instances.label: Manager walks the sales floor of a grocery/big-box/specialty store during trading hours and does greeting and wayfinding: acknowledging shoppers at the entrance or in an aisle, answering 'where do I find X?', pointing or walking them to the right aisle or department.

Substantive customer assistance on the floor: comparing two products for a shopper, checking whether a size/model is in stock, correcting a shelf-tag or price dispute, handling a complaint or a return question, pulling the right item off the shelf and placing it in the shopper's cart.

Shelf stocking/replenishment: pulling a U-boat or pallet of mixed cases from the backroom into a busy aisle, cutting cases, placing assorted packaged goods and produce onto shelves and endcaps to planogram, rotating and facing product, flattening cardboard and returning overstock.

Taking inventory: walking aisles to count and record on-hand stock, scanning shelves/tags for out-of-stocks, misplaced items and price errors, checking backroom overstock, and entering counts into the ordering/inventory system.

Retrieving stock for a waiting customer: checking the backroom or overstock shelf for a requested item, getting it down (ladder/high shelf), carrying it out to the customer or the front, and helping with a bulky item.
Front-end coverage during a rush: opening and running a register, bagging orders, retrieving carts from the lot, mopping a spill, straightening a display that shoppers have disordered.

sources.title: Simbe scales inventory robotics deal with BJ's Wholesale Club - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomous shelf-scanning robot performs inventory audits (stock levels, pricing, planogram, product location) on the sales floor of warehouse-club stores, deployed chainwide at BJ's Wholesale Club.

sources.title: Simbe upgrades vision platform with AI-powered capabilities - The Robot Report
sources.claim: As of 2025 Tally autonomously navigates open store aisles and scans shelves to find out-of-stocks, incorrect tags and misplaced items; deployed at additional US grocery chains (e.g., 17 Harmons stores, Oct 2025).

sources.system: Inventory Scan tower on BrainOS-powered Tennant scrubber
sources.title: Sam's Club Begins National Deployment of Automated Inventory Analytics Robots
sources.claim: Sam's Club completed a chainwide rollout of Brain Corp/Tennant Inventory Scan towers on ~600 autonomous floor scrubbers that capture shelf inventory data while driving the club floor and report stock levels and price accuracy to managers.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores (NVIDIA blog)
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA restocks refrigerated beverage shelves in FamilyMart convenience stores, running on an installed rail behind the cooler and placing drinks automatically over 98% of the time, with remote operators only for rare failures; deployed to 300 stores.

sources.title: Staples deploys RightHand Robotics tech in its fulfillment centers | Supply Chain Dive
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick autonomous piece-picking workcells pick assorted packaged retail goods presented in totes and place them into destination containers; deployed across Staples' North American fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic piece picking/put-away. It is the manipulation core of shelf replenishment - grasping assorted consumer packaged goods and placing them at a specified location - but only when goods and destination are presented to the machine in a fixtured cell, which is the E1 counterfactual for stocking.

sources.title: DHL to deploy 1,000 Boston Dynamics Robots in Warehouses | Supply Chain Magazine
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously handles and moves cases (unloading trailers/containers) in logistics facilities at DHL, at up to 700 cases per ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk case handling. Restocking begins with moving cases off pallets/trailers; Stretch does this autonomously where cases are presented in a structured, machine-oriented area, supporting only the E1 form of the stocking instance.

sources.title: Fellow Robots' NAVii autonomous retail robot helps Lowe's improve service - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Fellow Robots' NAVii/LoweBot, an autonomous retail service robot, operated in 11 Lowe's stores greeting shoppers, answering simple product-location questions in multiple languages and leading customers to the right shelf while also auditing inventory.

sources.title: LG Cloi GuideBot Enhances Customer Service at DFW | Aviation Pros
sources.claim: LG's CLOi GuideBot, a commercially available autonomous guide robot, provided customer service at Dallas Fort Worth International Airport - greeting travelers, answering questions by voice and escorting them via wayfinding in a busy public facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: greeting visitors and directing/escorting them to a location in an institution-controlled facility. Same interaction and navigation demands as greeting shoppers and pointing them to an aisle on a store floor.

sources.title: Walmart is rolling out its massive online pickup towers to 500 stores / Media mention - Cleveron
sources.claim: Cleveron's automated pickup towers, installed inside Walmart stores, retrieve a customer's specific order from internal fixtured storage and hand it over within seconds of the customer identifying themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetching a requested item from stock for a waiting customer. The machine locates and delivers the specified goods to the customer at the storefront, which is the fetch-from-back-stock instance when the stock is held in fixtured racking (the E1 counterfactual).

sources.title: Automated Drive-Up Grocery Kiosks Hit the Market | Winsight Grocery Business
sources.claim: Automated grocery pickup kiosks marketed by Bell and Howell hold up to 2,000 totes and deliver a customer's order at the storefront in as little as 45 ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving stored goods for a waiting customer. Confirms the pickup-tower class of machine is current and commercial, supporting the E1 form of the customer-fetch instance.

instances.label: After-hours interior intrusion/door alarm at a corporate office or logistics facility: manager (or on-call manager via the SOC) has the alarm point investigated — travel to the alarm location, look for signs of forced entry or persons, determine the usual benign cause (door held open, cleaning crew, badge error), document the event and clear the alarm.

Outdoor perimeter intrusion alarm at an industrial site, warehouse yard or campus: check the fence line/gate/yard where the alarm tripped, verify perimeter integrity and that doors and gates are secure, identify animals/weather/vehicles as cause, log and clear or escalate.

Fire alarm activation in an occupied office building or campus: go to the fire panel, identify the zone, verify smoke/heat vs. false alarm, initiate and oversee evacuation of employees to assembly points, sweep floors/restrooms for stragglers, meet and brief the responding fire department, then authorize re-entry and reset.

On-site medical emergency (employee collapse, seizure, fall, laceration): respond with first-aid kit and AED, assess the casualty, render first aid/CPR/AED, direct bystanders and clear the area, call and escort EMS to the patient, then complete the incident report.

Bomb threat call or suspicious package/unattended bag: run the threat-assessment checklist, direct occupants to search their own areas, decide on partial or full evacuation and relocation distance, cordon the item, liaise with police/EOD on arrival, and give the all-clear.

Emergency response in an uncontrolled or off-site setting: incident in a public-facing parking area or sidewalk adjacent to the property, at a construction/expansion zone, an outdoor event crowd, or an unstaffed remote site — layout unfamiliar, bystanders and weather uncontrolled, response improvised within procedure.

sources.transferJustification: Same task: physical response to an intrusion/door alarm inside a facility, including on-scene verification and incident documentation.

sources.claim: Ascento Guard autonomously patrols outdoor industrial sites, warehouses and pharma campuses, verifying perimeter integrity and checking that doors and windows are ..., and detecting people on the premises.
sources.transferJustification: Perimeter alarm verification is the physical core of responding to an outdoor intrusion alarm: reaching the alarm point, checking openings and reporting the cause.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine documented security round of the employer's own office building or corporate campus: walking floors, garage and lobby to verify perimeter/interior doors are secured, restricted rooms locked, no unauthorized persons after hours, egress paths clear, lighting, cameras and badge readers functioning; deficiencies logged in a report.

Exterior/perimeter inspection of an industrial, logistics or data-center site owned by the employer: fence line, gates, vehicle barriers, exterior lighting, dock and exterior door integrity, unauthorized vehicles or persons; deficiencies photographed and logged for follow-up.

Formal compliance inspection/audit of a facility against a regulation or written standard (e.g., NISPOM self-inspection of a cleared area, CFATS/TSA, PCI, healthcare accreditation security elements): checklist verification of container locks and key control, testing alarms and duress devices, verifying storage of sensitive material and access records, interviewing custodians, issuing written findings and corrective actions.

Multi-site inspection trip to remote locations (bank branches, retail stores, clinics, tenant suites, remote yards): travel to each site, walk it with local management, check safe/cash room, alarm panel and CCTV coverage, verify signage and posted procedures, write per-site findings.

Ad hoc or post-incident examination: after a break-in, alarm, tailgating complaint, or during renovation - physically test suspect doors, locks and hardware by hand, inspect roof, loading dock, mechanical and construction areas, judge whether policy or code was breached and what remediation is required.

Pre-occupancy or event security survey of an as-found property: prospective lease space, active construction site, or temporary event venue - walk the property, assess entry points, sightlines, barriers and lighting, and produce physical-security recommendations.

instances.label: Paper checks arrive by mail at the company office; the controller (or finance staff under the controller) opens envelopes, separates checks from remittance stubs, endorses them, logs the receipts against receivables, runs the batch through a desktop remote-deposit-capture scanner and transmits the deposit file to the bank. Ordinary office/mailroom conditions, mixed envelope types, occasional non-conforming items.

Cash receipts from registers, collection boxes or departmental cashiers are brought to a back office / cash room; currency and coin are counted and validated, reconciled to register or receipt reports, over/short recorded, deposit slip and bag prepared or the cash loaded into a safe for armored pickup.

The bank run: locked deposit bag with cash and checks is carried out of the building, driven or walked to the bank branch, night depository or deposit-taking ATM, deposited, and the receipt brought back and filed. Public streets, parking lots, varying bank premises, security/duress considerations.

In-person receipt at a counter or desk: a customer, tenant, member or donor hands over cash or a check; the worker verifies the amount and payee, issues a receipt, records the payment to the correct account, and secures the item in a till or safe pending deposit.

Off-site or event collections: cash boxes and checks from a fundraiser, fair booth, church collection, or satellite location are gathered, counted and reconciled in a non-standard space (banquet hall, tent, borrowed room), then secured and prepared for deposit.

instances.label: Routine safety walk-through of the production floor at the manager's own plant: traversing aisles and work cells during a shift, observing PPE use, machine guarding and interlock condition, housekeeping, blocked aisles/exits, slip and trip hazards and ergonomics; stopping to question operators and supervisors about what they observe, and recording findings with corrective actions and owners.

Scheduled formal compliance audit against a checklist (OSHA/EPA/ISO 14001 or 45001, corporate EHS standard): verifying training records, LOTO procedures, SDS binders, permit and waste-manifest logs, sampling records; interviewing operators to confirm written procedure matches practice; verifying prior findings were closed; issuing a written audit report with ratings.

Routine environmental-compliance rounds through process and utility areas: reading gauges and meters on pollution-control equipment (baghouse differential pressure, scrubber flow, wastewater pH), walking piping/tank/compressor areas looking for leaks, drips, spills, thermal anomalies and fugitive emissions, and logging readings and out-of-range conditions into the compliance record.

Functional verification of safety systems during an audit: testing emergency stops and light-curtain interlocks, flushing eyewash/safety showers, checking fire extinguisher tags and pressure, exit lights and alarms, verifying guards are in place and lockout devices applied, and signing off inspection tags.

Compliance check of hazardous waste and chemical storage areas: satellite accumulation drums (labels, accumulation start dates, closed lids, compatibility), secondary containment integrity, aisle spacing, spill kit stocking, drum condition, stormwater drains and outfalls; documenting deficiencies for the RCRA/stormwater file.

Audit of non-routine or contractor-controlled areas at the site: an in-plant construction or major turnaround zone, roof work, scaffolding, confined-space entry or hot-work permits, where layout changes daily, temporary equipment and unfamiliar crews are present, and hazards are novel each visit.

Focused verification visit at a subcontractor's plant: source/first-article inspection, line walk of a specific process, hands-on examination of parts and gauges, checking work instructions at the station, and verifying that a previously issued corrective action was implemented and is effective.

Pre-award assessment of a new or prospective subcontractor, frequently a small job shop or an overseas facility with an unfamiliar layout, mixed equipment condition and incomplete documentation; the auditor scores capability and quality-system maturity from what is found on site.

Remote/virtual or desk audit conducted from the QC manager's office: review of the supplier's submitted document package and self-assessment questionnaire, live video walkthrough guided by supplier staff, follow-up interviews, and a written audit report with risk rating.

instances.label: Routine walkdown of the powerhouse / turbine-generator building at a geothermal plant: following a fixed route past turbine, generator, lube-oil skids, condensate and brine pumps, heat exchangers and switchgear; reading local pressure/temperature/flow gauges and panel indicators, listening and feeling for abnormal vibration or noise, spotting oil or steam leaks, confirming each unit is in its expected operating state, and logging findings.

Outdoor balance-of-plant round inside the plant fence: cooling towers and fans, condensers, non-condensable gas removal system, brine/steam piping, valves, tanks, chemical injection skids and the yard/switchyard; visual and thermal checks for leaks, scaling, hot bearings, level and pressure readings, in weather, on gravel/steel walkways.

Routine round of production and injection wellheads on pads across the resource area: checking wellhead pressure and temperature gauges, valve positions, flowline and expansion-joint condition, steam/brine or H2S leakage, silica/calcite scaling signs, injection pump and flow meter operation; pads reached by unpaved service roads, layout varies pad to pad, exposure to weather, steam plumes and vegetation.

Traverse and inspection of the gathering system between pads: kilometers of two-phase steam/brine pipelines, expansion loops, supports, insulation, separators and knockout drums crossing open terrain; looking for leaks, sagging or shifted supports, ground subsidence, erosion, washed-out access roads and encroaching vegetation.

Non-routine investigative inspection after an alarm, trip, unusual reading, seismic event or operator report: going to the affected equipment in the plant or field, opening cabinets or insulation covers, using handheld instruments, checking valve lineups and local controls hands-on, diagnosing the cause with the maintenance crew and judging whether the unit may keep running.

Environmental, safety and compliance assessment across the well field: H2S/non-condensable gas and fugitive-emission monitoring, sump and secondary containment condition, spill or discharge checks, erosion and subsidence markers, road and fence condition, and post-storm damage assessment; findings feed regulatory reports.

Pre-job site assessment of an existing pad ahead of drilling, workover or major maintenance: pad surface and access road condition, laydown and rig-up space, wellhead and cellar access, utility and pipeline tie-in locations, hazards documented and communicated to the contractor.

Reconnaissance assessment of undeveloped acreage for field expansion: walk and map surface manifestations (fumaroles, hot springs, altered ground), assess geology, terrain, drainage and access for candidate well pad locations on unimproved public or leased land with no infrastructure.

Well-test and sampling round at the wellhead: hook up test gauges/orifice or weir-box instrumentation, draw steam-condensate and brine samples at sample points, check flow, silica/calcite scaling and chemistry indications, and record test conditions.

instances.label: Process-signal fault in the plant control building/instrument shop: a brine or steam pressure/temperature/level transmitter reads erratically or drops out. The manager trends the DCS, goes to the marshalling cabinet or junction box, injects/measures the 4-20 mA loop with a calibrator, finds a loose termination, blown loop fuse or failed transmitter, tightens/replaces it, recalibrates and verifies the signal in the control room.

Field instrument on outdoor plant equipment (separator, flash vessel, cooling tower, brine/NCG pump): plugged impulse line, failed thermocouple or vibration probe, corroded conduit/connector. Work at height on catwalks or in pipe racks, in heat, steam, rain and H2S-bearing atmosphere with hot pressurized lines nearby; clear or replace the sensing element, re-terminate wiring, confirm the reading.

Electrical fault in the MCC/switchgear room: a pump or fan motor trips repeatedly; the manager isolates and applies lockout/tagout, meters the circuit, finds a blown fuse, failed contactor/overload relay or heat-damaged termination, replaces the small component or re-torques the lug, resets the breaker and restarts the drive.

Wellfield/remote asset: wellhead pressure transmitter, RTU/telemetry link, solar panel-battery supply or damaged instrument cable on a well pad or along a cross-country steam line. Requires driving gravel roads to a varied, weather-exposed pad, diagnosing power/communication loss, and swapping a fuse, battery, antenna or transmitter in the field.

Control-system I/O trouble: nuisance alarms or a dead channel traced to a failed DCS/PLC input card, a tripped power supply or a loose field cable in the control cabinet. The manager verifies at the console, then opens the cabinet, reseats or hot-swaps the card, restores the power supply and confirms the point is healthy.

instances.label: Routine in-process liquid grab sample inside a corn-ethanol plant process building: the manager/operator walks to a sample cock on the slurry, liquefaction, fermenter or beer line (often on an elevated grated platform), cracks the valve, flushes the dead leg, fills and caps a labeled jar/vial of hot mash or beer, and carries it to the plant lab for HPLC/DP/pH checks.

Finished-product certification sampling at loadout: while denatured ethanol or B100 is loaded to a tanker truck or railcar, a sample is drawn from the loading-arm sample tap (or through the dome hatch), composited, sealed, labeled and sent/retained for the ASTM certificate of analysis before the load is released; outdoors at the rack, under time pressure.

Storage-tank sampling in the tank farm: climbing tank stairs to the hatch and lowering a bomb/thief sampler for upper-middle-lower samples of finished ethanol, biodiesel or feedstock oil, or drawing from side sample cocks; outdoors, weather, fall-protection and static/vapor precautions.

By-product sampling of solids and corn oil: grabbing DDGS/wet cake at the dryer discharge, a conveyor drop point or the loadout chute with a scoop or pelican, or from a loaded truck/hopper car, plus distillers corn oil from a tank or transfer line; hot, dusty, confined chute areas.

Biodiesel/renewable-diesel secondary streams: drawing crude glycerin, methanol-recovery, wash water or process water samples from sample valves on reactors, settling tanks and separators; viscous media, sometimes plugged or crystallizing ports needing purging before a valid sample is obtained.

Inspection of the fuel-handling train: conveyor galleries, transfer towers, screens, hogs/chippers, drag chains and silo/dome feeders — checking belt tracking, roller and bearing temperatures, spillage and dust accumulation (fire/explosion risk), guarding and dust-suppression, in a dusty, partly outdoor institution-controlled yard.

Fuel receiving/storage yard inspection proper: walking the chip or bark pile with front-end loaders and delivery trucks moving, probing/feeling fuel for moisture, fines and contamination (rock, metal, plastic), checking pile temperatures and self-heating, drainage and housekeeping, and directing loader operators.

Inspection of the plant's electrical station/switchyard or interconnect substation: transformers, breakers, bushings, disconnects, cable terminations and the generator step-up unit — thermal/visual checks for hot connections, oil leaks and levels, silica gel/desiccant color, fence, grounding and signage; energized outdoor fenced yard in all weather.

Safety and compliance field walkthrough: verifying lockout/tagout tags and permits with the crew on an outage job, checking PPE use, guarding, confined-space and hot-work controls, fire protection equipment, housekeeping and spill containment, engaging operators and contractors about hazards, correcting deficiencies on the spot and signing off the inspection record.

Field investigation of an abnormal condition or alarm (boiler trip, high vibration, plugged ash chute, fuel-feed jam, unusual smell or noise): manager goes to the equipment, opens cabinets or inspection doors, feels and listens to machinery, checks local indicators and sight glasses, may climb ladders or enter tight spaces, judges whether it is safe to keep running and directs immediate corrective action.

Hands-on fault troubleshooting with the electrician: a conveyor or pump motor will not start or keeps tripping; de-energize and LOTO, open the MCC bucket, test the control circuit, contactor, overload and motor leads with multimeter and megger, replace the failed contactor, relay or fuse with hand tools, re-land and torque conductors, retest and return to service.

Corrective electrical repair out in the fuel-handling, conveyor, ash or boiler areas: dusty, hot, cramped, often from a ladder or platform - replacing chafed motor leads, a burned junction box or drag-chain cable, a damaged limit switch or proximity sensor, re-supporting conduit, then continuity and insulation checks before restart.

Planned-outage electrical maintenance: LOTO the bus, rack out breakers, vacuum and clean cubicles and bus, inspect and lubricate mechanisms, torque bus and lug connections to spec, run insulation-resistance, contact-resistance and trip/relay tests on breakers, transformers and generator leads, then reassemble, rack in and re-energize.

Small installation or modification work: mounting and wiring a new control panel, instrument loop or distribution circuit - landing conductors on terminal blocks and breakers, ferruling and labeling, point-to-point continuity and megger verification before energizing.

instances.label: Control-room console work at a 15-75 MW wood-fired stoker/fluidized-bed plant: the manager (covering a shift or overseeing a planned evolution) uses the DCS/HMI to bring the unit up after an outage or shut it down - sequencing ID/FD fans, feedwater pumps, fuel feeders, lighting the start-up burners, raising steam, rolling and synchronizing the turbine-generator, or reversing the sequence for shutdown.

Routine regulation while the unit runs: adjusting load/steam setpoints to follow dispatch or a steam host, trimming fuel feed rate, grate/bed speed, combustion air and drum level as wood fuel moisture and sizing vary, managing bed temperature and emissions limits - all from the control room over a shift.

Field operation of auxiliaries inside the plant: walking the boiler house, fuel yard and ash system to start/stop pumps, fans, conveyors, screws and ash handling at local panels, throw hand switches and breakers, line up or throttle manual handwheel valves, and reset tripped drives after a jam or plug.

Small packaged bioenergy unit (containerized wood-gasifier genset or institutional wood-chip boiler/CHP at a campus, sawmill or district heating site): starting the unit on heat/power demand, modulating output, and stopping it, with automatic ignition, fuel feed and ... removal, and remote monitoring.

Protective/emergency stop on an instrumented abnormal condition: loss of flame, high/low drum level, overpressure, high furnace draft, turbine vibration or overspeed, grid disturbance - controls operated to trip and safely shut down the boiler, turbine or fuel system.

Judgment-driven intervention on conditions instrumentation does not capture: smoke or odor from a conveyor, unusual noise or slagging seen through a sight port, an off-spec fuel delivery causing erratic combustion, contractor work in progress - the manager decides to override automatic control, derate, isolate equipment or shut down, then restores the unit.

Inspection of the outdoor switchyard/high-voltage yard: walk the fenced yard checking transformers, breakers, disconnects, bushings, arresters and bus work for hot spots, oil level and leaks, corrosion, cracked insulators, animal/vegetation intrusion and fence/security damage; energized equipment with approach-distance limits, all weather including snow, ice and rain.

Inspection of the control house / relay house: check protection and control panels, annunciator and alarm indications, SCADA/RTU and communication racks, station battery bank and chargers, HVAC and room temperature, lighting, cleanliness and access; indoor, standard building, doors and thresholds to negotiate.

Safety-standards compliance walkthrough of the plant: verify crews' and contractors' PPE use and safe work practices, lockout/tagout tags and clearances, machine guarding and barricades, fire extinguisher and fire-system tags, confined-space and hot-work permits, signage and egress, spill containment; interview workers, judge conditions against OSHA/utility standards, and write findings and corrective actions.

Outdoor round of the dam, waterway and grounds: dam crest and downstream face, spillway and gate structures, intake and trash racks, tailrace, penstock alignment, access roads, drainage and seepage points, erosion, debris and vegetation; taken-as-found terrain, water, weather and wildlife, layout differing by site.

instances.label: Routine switching and load/voltage control executed from the plant control room or a centralized operations center: synchronizing a hydro unit to the grid, opening/closing generator and line breakers, adjusting excitation/VARs and taps to hold schedule voltage, following dispatcher orders and logging each step per the switching procedure. Energized 13.8 kV-230 kV equipment; commands go to motor-operated switchgear via the plant/substation automation (SCADA/HMI) system.

Executing a switching order in the switchyard or switchgear room to isolate equipment for maintenance and later restore it: operating manual/motor disconnects, racking out a breaker, verifying the device is open and dead with a tester, applying portable safety grounds, hanging tags and barriers, then issuing/holding the clearance for the crew and reversing the sequence afterward. Full arc-flash PPE, outdoor yard or indoor gear room, two-person verification.

Routine inspection round of the energized substation: walking the yard and gear room, reading gauges and meters, checking transformer oil level/temperature, SF6 pressure, bushings, insulators, battery/DC system, listening for corona or arcing, taking infrared thermography of connections, and logging readings and exceptions.

Routine abnormal event: a protective relay trips a line or unit breaker (fault, lightning, overload). Acknowledge alarms and relay targets, isolate the faulted section, reclose or reconfigure to restore service, coordinate with the transmission dispatcher, and document. No equipment damage; standard, pre-planned recovery.

Complex abnormal event: transformer or breaker failure, storm damage, loss of station service or black-start conditions. Requires field investigation of the energized/de-energized yard, damage assessment, improvised reconfiguration outside the pre-planned schemes, and directing crews under time pressure.

Planned outage coordination on the transmission interface: taking a main transformer, station bus or transmission line out of service and returning it, including pre-outage switching, phase and polarity verification, protective relay in/out-of-service changes, energization checks and load-carrying tests with maintenance and relay crews on site.

The physical acts (breakers, disconnectors, earthing switches) are performed by motor operators under the substation automation system after a single supervisory command, with automated status and interlock verification replacing the operator's step-by-step manual execution.

sources.developer: Industry practice (multiple relay vendors), per Electrical Engineering Portal
sources.title: The art of generator synchronization techniques that every true engineer MUST know about

sources.transferJustification: Related sub-capability of the same task: closing an energized generator breaker onto the transmission bus. Automatic synchronizers make the phase/voltage/slip decision and issue the close themselves, which is the physical act the plant operator would otherwise perform.

instances.label: Routine daily/weekly walkthrough of a distribution center or warehouse floor: checking housekeeping, blocked aisles and exits, spills and roof/pipe leaks, damaged racking and pallets, dock doors and levelers, floor and lighting condition; noting deficiencies and issuing repair work orders.

Fleet condition inspection at a terminal, yard or delivery station: walking tractors, trailers or delivery vans to check tires, lights, body and underbody damage, fluid leaks and brake condition, verifying driver-reported defects, and ordering shop repairs or replacements.

Scheduled condition checks of fixed material-handling and facility equipment: conveyors and sortation, motors, compressors, battery-charging areas, refrigeration units and dock equipment; looking/listening for wear, heat, leaks and vibration and triggering preventive maintenance or repair.

Ad hoc investigation of a specific breakdown or damage event (conveyor fault, refrigeration alarm, forklift damage, struck rack bay, roof leak after a storm): assessing the damage up close, deciding repair versus replacement, engaging a vendor and verifying the completed work.

Periodic formal safety/compliance walk, visual portion: verifying fire extinguishers are present, unobstructed and charged, exits and sprinkler clearances are clear, aisles marked, PPE and storage practices correct.

Periodic formal safety/compliance walk, functional and documentation portion: testing emergency lighting, eyewash and alarms, opening cabinets to verify first-aid and spill-kit contents, ordering third-party testing, and signing/filing the compliance record.

tasks.label: Collect and record growth, production, and environmental data.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Row-crop farm: manager walks or drives fields on a schedule through the season to collect crop growth data — emergence/stand counts, growth stage, plant height, weed/insect/disease pressure, moisture stress — photographing and logging observations by field and zone into a farm-management record. Open fields, variable weather, mud, terrain, wildlife.

Georeferenced soil (and occasionally tissue) sampling across fields on grids or management zones: pulling multiple cores per point to a set depth, bagging and labeling, logging GPS coordinates, submitting to a lab and recording results into fertility/nutrient records. Done in stubble or bare fields, often cold and wet.

Harvest-season production data on grain/row crops: yield-monitor calibration and per-field yield, moisture and area capture during harvest, plus grain-cart/weigh-wagon loads, truck and elevator tickets and bin inventory, reconciled and recorded as per-field production records.

Greenhouse or nursery: recording crop growth measurements (height, leaf/flower/fruit counts, quality grade), crop inventory counts by bench or row, and environmental data (temperature, RH, CO2, light, irrigation EC/pH) logged into production and climate records.

Dairy or other confined-livestock operation: capturing per-animal production and growth data — milk weights and components per cow per milking, feed intake, body weight, health/activity events — and recording them in herd-management software inside the barn/parlor.

Beef cow-calf/stocker ranch: collecting animal growth and production data — birth/weaning/yearling weights and body condition at the working chute or scale, EID/tag reads, calving and pregnancy records — plus pasture forage and rain-gauge readings on range and pasture taken as found.

instances.label: Salmonid hatchery run/trap season: manager oversees returning adults entering the hatchery ladder, trap or holding pond - fish are counted, sorted (hatchery vs wild, male/female, ripe vs green), moved into holding ponds or hauled by truck, and records kept. Hatchery grounds, agency-controlled, seasonal high fish volume.

Egg-take / spawning day at the hatchery spawning shed: manager directs and works a crew - anesthetize or euthanize ripe females, check ripeness, strip or cut out eggs, collect milt, dry-fertilize, water-harden, disinfect, estimate and record egg numbers, cull unripe fish. Slippery, wet, biosecure work area.

Egg incubation monitoring: daily rounds of the incubation building (vertical-stack trays, hatching jars, upwelling incubators) - check water flow, temperature units and alarms, treat for fungus, shock eggs, pick and enumerate dead and unfertilized eggs, decide eye-up and ponding/transfer timing.

Fry and fingerling rearing oversight in hatchery tanks and raceways: set and adjust feed type/rate, watch feeding response and behavior, sample-weigh for growth and condition, monitor DO and water quality, pick mortalities, direct cleaning, oversee grading, counting, splitting and transfer of fish.

Remote field collection of broodstock: running a stream weir, picket trap or seine at an off-site location in field conditions (debris, changing flows, weather), checking and clearing the trap, sorting and loading fish for haul to the hatchery.

instances.label: Egg-stage work to raise hatch rates at a salmonid/trout hatchery: pulling incubator trays, shocking eyed eggs, picking or machine-sorting out dead (white) eggs, enumerating and re-loading eggs into incubators, and checking incubation temperature and flow. Indoor incubation room, standard stacked trays/jars, millions of eggs per season.

Daily feeding program to improve growth: setting and adjusting rations for fry/fingerlings across dozens to hundreds of tanks or raceways by size, species and water temperature, distributing feed on schedule, watching feed response and waste, refilling hoppers and cleaning feeders. Indoor RAS/flow-through hatchery hall or outdoor raceway bank.

Life-support and water-quality rounds that drive growth and health: reading dissolved oxygen, temperature, pH and ammonia across tanks, adjusting flows, oxygen injection and alarms, backwashing/cleaning filters and tank screens, and removing accumulated mortalities and solids from tank bottoms. Company-run hatchery building with fixed piping and standard tanks.

Fish-handling events to improve uniformity, growth and disease resistance: crowding and pumping fish out of tanks, size grading, counting, vaccinating smolts/fingerlings, and transferring graded groups to new tanks or transport trucks. A few times per production cycle, with pumps, graders, counters and vaccination lines set up on the hatchery floor.

Health surveillance and disease response: daily observation of behaviour and appearance, netting and examining moribund fish, gross necropsy/wet mounts, sending samples to a fish-health lab, consulting the veterinarian, mixing and administering therapeutic baths or medicated feed, and disinfecting tanks, nets and equipment between batches. Hatchery tanks, wet lab and equipment room.

Devising improvements: reviewing survival, growth and mortality records; designing and running side-by-side trials (new diet, altered incubation temperature, stocking density, egg-disinfection protocol); marking, weighing and sampling trial groups; rewriting SOPs and biosecurity plans; training and directing hatchery staff. Office plus hands-on set-up of trial tanks in the hatchery.

instances.label: Ranch/field infrastructure round: driving or walking fence lines, gates, cattle guards, stock tanks, water pipelines, culverts and farm roads over uneven pasture in all weather; splicing broken wire, resetting a leaning post, re-hanging a gate, clearing/patching a leaking float valve or pipe.

Mobile machinery service in the farm shop or yard: pre-season and between-job inspection of tractors, combines, sprayers, trucks and implements — walkaround for leaks, worn belts/chains, cracked welds, loose bolts, tire condition — then greasing fittings, changing oil/filters, replacing a hose, belt or bearing, welding a broken bracket.

Poultry breeder operation: manager coordinates selection and grading of breeder pullets and males for uniformity and soundness, sets male-to-female ratios and spiking, and maintains the breeder flock (restricted feeding programs, weighing samples, lighting, health program) in a controlled breeder house.

Small or diversified livestock operation (horses, sheep, goats, small beef seedstock): manager evaluates and buys broodmares/rams/bucks/bulls at sales or on farm, hands-on appraisal of conformation, teeth, udders and soundness, and maintains the brood animals in mixed barns, paddocks and pastures of varied layout with variable weather.

instances.label: In-season scouting round of broadacre row crops (corn, soybeans, wheat, cotton): the manager drives field roads and walks into several representative spots, checks stand and growth stage, looks for leaf lesions and insect feeding, counts pests against economic thresholds, and decides whether a fungicide/insecticide pass is warranted. Cultivated, farm-owned field planted in uniform rows; weather and mud vary.

Greenhouse or nursery crop inspection: walking benches/bays of ornamentals, young plants or vegetables, checking sticky cards and undersides of foliage for thrips, aphids, mites and mildew, flagging hot spots for IPM treatment, and judging which batches are finished/salable. Indoor facility with fixed aisles, rails or concrete/gravel floors, controlled access.

Orchard or vineyard harvest-maturity inspection: sampling fruit through the block (color, size, firmness, brix/starch), often with a refractometer or penetrometer, while also spotting mildew, rots, mites or borers, then setting the pick date. Trellised/planted rows on farm-controlled ground.

Harvest-readiness walk of berry or fruiting-vegetable fields (strawberry beds, tomatoes, melons, peppers): judging per-fruit ripeness and fruit load across the block to schedule picks and check for damage or pest injury. Open, farm-managed field in planted beds/rows.

Harvest-readiness inspection of head/root crops (lettuce, broccoli, potatoes, onions): cutting heads open, pulling or digging plants to check tuber size, skin set, internal quality and root/soil pests before scheduling harvest or vine kill. Open farm field, requires destructive sampling and digging.

Inspection in unstructured land: pasture/hay/rangeland forage condition, timber tracts for bark beetle or defoliator damage, remote or flooded blocks (rice, cranberry), and post-hail/storm damage walkthroughs; also digging roots and soil pits for grubs, nematodes or root rot sampling. Terrain taken as found, no maintained working standard.

instances.label: Beef cow-calf or stocker operator checks the herd on pasture or rangeland (horseback, ATV, or pickup): walking/riding through scattered cattle, looking for pinkeye, footrot, scours, bloat, lice/tick loads, respiratory signs, poor body condition, and problem calvings; terrain, brush, weather and animal flight distance vary daily.

Cattle brought into corrals and run through a squeeze chute/headgate for individual hands-on examination — processing/preconditioning days, sick-pen pulls, veterinarian-supervised herd health checks: temperature, eyes, mouth, feet, udder, palpation, skin scrapes for mange/lice, fecal or blood sampling, with the manager conducting or supervising a crew.

Dairy herd health screening at milking in a freestall barn/parlor or robotic milking barn: checking udders and foremilk for clinical mastitis, watching for lameness and off-feed/ketotic cows, reviewing flags, drafting suspect cows for closer examination or vet attention.

Broiler, turkey, or layer house daily flock walk-through: moving through tens of thousands of birds to spot sick, lame, or culled-out birds and mortality, and reading disease signs such as abnormal droppings, coughing/snicking, wet litter, or mite infestation on birds and equipment.

Hog barn (sow, nursery, or finisher) daily inspection: walking pen alleys and crates, listening for coughing, checking for scours, lameness, hernias, mange/lice, off-feed pigs; marking or pulling affected pigs for treatment.

Sheep or goat flock parasite and disease check on pasture or in a catch pen: catching and restraining animals to score conjunctival color (FAMACHA) for barber pole worm, checking body condition, feet for footrot/scald, and collecting fecal samples for egg counts.

instances.label: Large Midwest row-crop operation (corn/soybeans, 1,000-5,000 acres): the farmer-manager directs the tillage and planting campaign — laying out field passes and prescriptions on mapped fields, hitching and setting tillage tools and planters, running/dispatching tractors across a compressed spring window, and adjusting depth, speed and timing for soil moisture and weather.

Row-crop nutrient and crop-protection passes: after scouting, the manager directs herbicide/fungicide spraying and fertilizer application — timing the window, mixing and loading product, running the sprayer or applicator (or a spray drone/custom applicator) over mapped fields, managing drift and re-entry, and keeping application records.

Grain and oilseed harvest: the manager directs combining of standing corn/soybeans/wheat — running or supervising the combine, monitoring moisture, losses and settings, coordinating grain carts and trucks to bins or elevator, and sequencing fields against weather.

Orchard, vineyard and other perennial specialty operations, machine work: the manager directs air-blast spraying, mowing/floor management, tillage and in-field transport through tree and vine rows on a trellised, institution-maintained block.

Labor-intensive specialty and diversified vegetable production: the manager directs (and often personally performs) hand transplanting, hand weeding/thinning, pruning, and repeated selective hand harvest of berries, tree fruit, or a dozen mixed vegetable crops on small irregular plots for fresh/direct market.

Greenhouse/nursery crop production: the manager directs seeding, transplanting and spacing, irrigation/fertigation, pest control, and picking of tomatoes or container stock inside a climate-controlled house with fixed aisles, benches and pipe-rail rows.

Rancher/livestock manager monitors breeding and animal handling: heat detection and AI or bull turnout, calving checks, working cattle through corrals and chutes, ensuring handlers follow low-stress handling and drug-withdrawal/record rules and stay safe around animals. Rangeland pastures, dirt corrals, portable panels, night checks.

Dairy manager monitors milking in the parlor or robot barn: teat prep and hygiene, milk quality against bulk-tank standards (abnormal/antibiotic milk kept out), wash and sanitation cycles, tank temperature, equipment function, and worker practices in the parlor. Fixed-layout facility with standard equipment, wet floors, cows moving through.

Manager monitors grading, sorting and packing of harvested product in the packing shed or grading room: product graded to size/color/defect standards, cull rates, sanitation and food-safety practice, and worker safety around conveyors, elevators and forklifts.

instances.label: Greenhouse/nursery manager walks the growing houses daily: reads and cross-checks climate (temperature, humidity, VPD, light, CO2), checks irrigation/fertigation emitters and drainage, and scouts benches or rows for pests, disease, nutrient deficiency and growth uniformity, producing a record of problem spots and orders to adjust set-points or treat.

Row-crop or orchard manager scouts fields through the season: stand/plant counts, weed, insect and disease pressure, nutrient deficiency symptoms, soil moisture and drainage, and function of pivots/drip lines — feeding decisions on irrigation, spray timing and harvest readiness.

Rangeland/pasture cattle manager checks stock and range across large, uneven, unfenced-interior country: locating and counting the herd, spotting sick, injured or calving animals, verifying water tanks and troughs, fence lines, and forage/grazing condition.

Aquaculture manager monitors ponds, tanks or net pens: dissolved oxygen, temperature, pH/ammonia across sampling points, aerator function, feeding response and fish behavior/health, adjusting aeration, feed or water exchange to keep stock in optimum conditions.

tasks.label: Inspect or review projects to monitor compliance with building and safety codes or other regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine safety-compliance walk of an active jobsite (weekly or daily): checking fall protection at leading edges and floor openings, scaffold erection/tagging, ladder use, excavation protection, electrical cords/GFCI, housekeeping and trip hazards, PPE and work practices; photographing and logging violations and directing trade foremen to correct them. Live crews, equipment, mud, changing layout.

Verification of installed work before cover-up or a milestone: rebar size/spacing/cover and embeds before a concrete pour, MEP rough-in in walls and ceiling plenums, hangers and seismic bracing, firestopping — checked with tape measure and approved drawings, then signed off for pour or for the AHJ inspection.

Life-safety and code walk of enclosed, near-complete interiors near turnover: egress path widths and door hardware, ADA clearances and mounting heights, rated assembly penetrations, exit signage, plus punch-list defects in finishes. Building enclosed but still a jobsite with stored materials and trades finishing.

Preparing for and accompanying municipal/third-party inspectors and special inspectors: reconciling permits, submittals, test reports and certifications against field conditions, walking the inspector through the work, and closing out cited deficiencies.

Review of off-site fabrication before shipment at a precast, structural-steel or modular plant: checking fabricated panels, cages, weldments or modules against approved shop drawings and code (dimensions, embeds, welds, connections) in the fabricator's controlled facility.

instances.label: Writing a project-specific construction quality control plan before/at contract award: reading the specs and contract quality requirements, building inspection and test plans, submittal and materials-testing registers, defining acceptance criteria, assigning QC roles, and getting the plan approved by the owner or agency (e.g., USACE-style CQC plan).

Running the three-phase control process for each definable feature of work: holding preparatory and initial-phase meetings with the subcontractor foreman and superintendent, reviewing shop drawings/submittals and mock-up expectations, agreeing on workmanship standards, and documenting the meeting and follow-up checks.

Day-to-day implementation during construction: reviewing daily QC reports and inspection checklists submitted by superintendents/QC technicians, scheduling and coordinating third-party materials testing (concrete cylinders, soil compaction, weld/bolt testing), reviewing lab reports, mill certificates and special-inspection reports for conformance.

Nonconformance and corrective action: logging deficiencies observed on walkthroughs or reported by inspectors, issuing nonconformance reports and rework directives to subcontractors, tracking closeout of corrective actions, and managing punch lists and quality documentation at turnover/commissioning.

Company- or program-level QC development: standardizing checklists and procedures across projects, training field staff and subcontractors on the quality program, auditing project compliance with the program, and revising procedures based on lessons learned, warranty claims, or owner/ISO 9001 requirements.

instances.label: Schedule-slip investigation on a large commercial/institutional project (office, hospital, data center): the CM walks the lagging area to establish what is actually installed versus the plan and model, identifies which trade/area is behind and by how much, photographs/scans conditions, and documents the deviation for the weekly schedule review.

Delay investigation whose cause is people or logistics: crew undermanned, material delivery late, inspection hold or unanswered RFI, equipment down, weather stoppage. The CM walks the work face, questions the sub's foreman and superintendent, checks delivery tickets, daily logs and inspection records, fixes the cause and directs a recovery plan.

Damage or non-conforming installed work found on an active commercial jobsite (water intrusion in finished drywall, cracked/spalled slab, conduit or sprinkler line damaged by another trade, out-of-tolerance framing). The CM goes to the spot, examines it up close, lifts covers/probes/measures, traces the source, decides which procedure was violated and by whom, directs rework and documents for backcharge.

Jobsite accident, near miss or property-damage incident (fall, struck-by, scaffold or excavation failure, equipment strike, crane incident). The CM secures the scene, inspects equipment, fall protection, shoring and permits, photographs, interviews the injured worker and witnesses, determines root cause and OSHA reportability, writes the incident report and issues corrective actions.

Residential or small-project variant (custom home, remodel, small tenant fit-out, occupied home): homeowner or client reports damage or a stalled schedule. The CM visits the occupied house/small site, inspects the complaint area, talks with the homeowner and the trade, determines cause and directs the fix.

sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated as-built verification/progress tracking. The output (which scope is behind, what was installed wrong) is the finding a CM's delay walk is meant to produce.

sources.title: Top 10: AI Tools in Construction | Construction Digital
sources.claim: Doxel remains in commercial use with contractors (DPR, Layton, Sundt) and its analytics flagged a trade slowdown early enough for the contractor ... add a crew; site capture is by autonomous robots or handheld devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated schedule-deviation detection; it is the delay-investigation finding itself (which work is behind, where, by how much) delivered from robot-captured site data.

sources.title: Tilbury Douglas becomes first contractor to launch a humanoid robot on a construction site
sources.claim: A tier-one contractor deployed a humanoid robot on a ... that autonomously navigates the site to capture 360-degree imagery ... progress reports, feeding health-and-safety monitoring and reporting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous site walk and documentation on an unstructured live jobsite, showing the traverse-and-record element of an investigation is achievable at E3.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan for Documenting Evidence for Public Safety | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio drones autonomously execute a 3D scan of a crash or incident scene after an on-site operator selects the scan volume, producing court-ready documentation; interpretation of the scene remains with human investigators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = accident-scene documentation. It covers imaging an incident scene but not securing the scene, inspecting equipment, interviewing witnesses, or determining root cause.

sources.system: ANYmal with gas leak and presence detection
sources.title: ANYbotics launches Gas Leak and Presence Detection for ANYmal inspection robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: ANYmal runs autonomous inspection missions in industrial plants and can localize and quantify pressurized gas leaks, alerting personnel in real time.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous anomaly localization inside a structured facility (E2). It shows fault detection on plant equipment, not investigation of damage to installed construction work with cause attribution and corrective direction.

instances.label: Director steps in to lead a preschool classroom session for 15-20 children aged 3-5 (covering an absent teacher or teaching a scheduled class): circle time, read-aloud, songs, guiding a hands-on activity, managing transitions and behavior, and maintaining line-of-sight safety supervision in a licensed center classroom.

Direct care in the infant/toddler room: diapering and changing soiled clothes, bottle- or spoon-feeding, lifting, holding and soothing a crying infant, placing children down for naps and monitoring them, sanitizing surfaces and hands between children.

Daily hygiene and mealtime routines with toddlers and preschoolers: serving snack/lunch, helping children eat and cleaning up spills, toileting and potty-training assistance, handwashing, wiping faces, putting on and taking off coats and shoes.

Supervising outdoor playground or indoor gross-motor time: monitoring a mixed group on climbers, swings and riding toys, spotting and lifting children, redirecting unsafe play, applying a bandage and ice for a scraped knee, head counts in and out.

Small-group or one-to-one instruction: leading a letters/numbers/shapes activity with manipulatives, an art or sensory-table project, or reading with an individual child, handing out and collecting materials, and recording developmental observations.

Behavior and incident response: physically separating two children in a biting/hitting conflict, holding and calming an escalated or distressed child, comforting an injured child until a parent arrives, and leading children through a fire or lockdown drill.

sources.system: Peer-like social robot playmate (Tega-class) in preschool storytelling study
sources.developer: MIT Media Lab Personal Robots Group
sources.title: A Long-Term Study of Young Children's Rapport, Social Emulation, and Language Learning With a Peer-Like Robot Playmate in Preschool
sources.claim: Social robots used in real preschools are deployed for short one-to-one learning games with an individual child alongside, not in place of, the teacher; a two-month field study with 17 children involved 8 storytelling sessions per child.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led early-literacy play with preschoolers. It shows the current ceiling of robots with this age group is a seated one-to-one language game, which does not carry over to leading a class group or to any physical caregiving (lifting, diapering, feeding, safety supervision).

sources.system: SPARC (Supervised Progressively Autonomous Robot Competencies) robot tutor
sources.developer: University of Plymouth with University of Lincoln and UWE
sources.title: Robots can learn how to support teachers in class sessions - University of Plymouth
sources.claim: A classroom robot tutor was first controlled by a human teacher and, after about three hours of learning, could support individual pupils in that one educational activity autonomously; it is framed as support for teachers, not replacement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot tutoring support in a classroom. Autonomy is limited to giving advice within a single pre-taught tabletop activity with a teacher present; it does not extend to running a whole class session, transitions, behavior management, or physical care.

sources.title: Robots For Autism Teach Human Emotion - RoboKind
sources.claim: Commercially deployed education robots for children run scripted social-skills lesson modules one-to-one with a human facilitator operating the session; several hundred units are in schools.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered instruction to children in a school. Milo is a torso-mounted humanoid delivering curriculum modules to one seated student with an adult facilitator; it cannot supervise a group, move children, or perform caregiving, so it does not substantiate completing any instance of this task.

sources.title: Day care facilities test robots as high-tech solution to alleviate staffing shortages - The Japan Times
sources.claim: Childcare-center robot pilots in Japan are limited to greeting, identifying children and taking temperatures, with nap monitoring done by cot sensors rather than by a robot providing care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot deployment inside a licensed nursery. The functions demonstrated (greeting, ID, thermography, sensor-based nap monitoring) are record-keeping aids, not direct care, so they do not substantiate feeding, diapering, soothing or supervising children.

sources.system: Social robots in PreK-12 classrooms (review of 23 field studies)

sources.claim: A review of field-based studies of social robots in real classrooms found feasibility but persistent difficulty sustaining long-term use, with robots positioned as supplements to teachers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robots teaching in school classrooms. The literature base documents short, adult-supervised, single-activity deployments, confirming no cited system runs a class session or provides direct care end to end.

instances.label: Bench-scale pretreatment screen in the company/lab R&D wet-chemistry lab: milled lignocellulosic feedstock (corn stover, sorghum, wood, bagasse) weighed into sealed tubes or small reactors, dosed with dilute acid, alkali, solvent/ionic liquid or hot water, heated for set times/temperatures, then washed/neutralized, enzymatically hydrolyzed, sampled and assayed for sugar release; conditions varied across a designed matrix.

Analytical characterization supporting the experiments, in the lab: compositional analysis of feedstock and pretreated solids/liquors (moisture, ash, extractives, two-stage hydrolysis, HPLC sugars/inhibitors), NIR calibration checks, and for biodiesel feedstocks oil titration for free fatty acids, water content, viscosity; standard glassware, ovens, balances and benchtop instruments.

Pilot / process-development-unit campaign in an institutionally controlled pilot facility: tens to hundreds of kilograms of feedstock loaded into hoppers, fed through a continuous or batch pretreatment reactor (steam explosion, dilute-acid, deacetylation), steam and chemical dosing set, periodic slurry sampling through ports, plug clearing, shutdown, washout and mass balance.

Receipt and preparation of bulk feedstock for experiments in a prep bay/high-bay: opening bags/bales or drums, drying, chipping and knife-milling, sieving to size fractions, riffle-splitting and labeling subsamples, moisture determination and storage; dusty, fibrous, variable material.

Off-site experimental work: sampling feedstock at a farm field, storage yard, elevator or waste-oil supplier, or running trial batches on a partner's equipment at a commercial plant; layout and conditions taken as found, weather and site traffic uncontrolled.

tasks.label: Conduct experiments to test new or alternate feedstock fermentation processes.

instances.label: Bench-scale screening experiment in an R&D lab: a candidate feedstock (e.g., corn-stover or sorghum hydrolysate, waste-stream sugar) is fermented in parallel shake flasks or microtiter/microbioreactor plates with several microbial strains and media variants; media prep, inoculation, timed sampling, OD/pH tracking and sugar/ethanol assays over 1-3 days.

Controlled benchtop bioreactor run (roughly 0.25-10 L) on a candidate feedstock in the process-development lab: vessel assembly/sterilization, probe calibration, charging feedstock/media, inoculation, fed-batch feeding, pH/DO/antifoam control, periodic aseptic sampling over 3-7 days, harvest and cleanout.

Preparing and characterizing the alternate feedstock ahead of fermentation: drying/milling biomass, weighing, acid/alkaline/steam pretreatment, enzymatic hydrolysis, neutralization/detoxification, and compositional/sugar analysis to define the substrate for the fermentation trial.

Pilot- or demonstration-scale fermentation trial (roughly 100-2,000 L) on the new feedstock at a pilot plant: slurry/media charging from totes, hose and filter hookups, SIP/CIP, inoculum train transfer, multi-day monitoring with shift sampling, harvest and downstream sample handoff.

Analytical characterization of the fermentation samples: filtering/diluting broth, preparing vials and plates, running HPLC/GC for sugars, organic acids and ethanol, cell-dry-weight/OD measurement, and compiling the run data for the experiment report.

tasks.label: Perform protein functional analysis and engineering for processing of feedstock and creation of biofuels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine functional characterization of candidate enzymes (cellulases/hemicellulases, lipases, esterases) against feedstock-derived substrates in the company or institute R&D lab: dilution series, microplate hydrolysis assays on milled/pretreated biomass or oil, incubation, reducing-sugar or HPLC quantification, activity/kinetics and pH-temperature optima worked up into a data package.

A round of enzyme engineering: designing mutations, building the variant library (mutagenesis, cloning, transformation), picking colonies, expressing variants in 96-deep-well plates, screening for improved activity or thermostability on the feedstock substrate, confirming and sequencing hits - on the bench and screening instruments of a standard molecular-biology lab.

Milligram-scale production and purification of a few selected variants for detailed characterization: expression cultures, harvest and lysis, affinity (His/tag) purification, SDS-PAGE and concentration checks, then kinetic and stability measurements on purified protein.

Application-relevant testing of the engineered protein in the process context: bench/small-pilot bioreactor runs of enzymatic saccharification of hydrolysate or fermentation with the engineered strain, controlled pH/temperature/feeding, time-course sampling and sugar/product analysis, in the company pilot or process-development facility.

Non-routine bench work: developing or validating a new assay for an unfamiliar feedstock or enzyme class, troubleshooting failed expression or interfering matrix effects, adapting protocols and improvising with shared lab instruments, running one-off exploratory experiments whose protocol does not yet exist.

tasks.label: Design or execute solvent or product recovery experiments in laboratory or field settings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Design-only work at a desk in the R&D office: choose candidate solvents and recovery routes, build a DOE matrix (solvent:oil ratio, temperature, vacuum, reflux, residence time), specify apparatus and analytical methods (GC/HPLC, Karl Fischer, ASTM specs), write the protocol and safety review, then interpret returned data and write the recovery/mass-balance report. No physical handling.

Bench-scale solvent/product recovery screening in an R&D chemistry lab: dozens of small (1-50 mL) parallel trials varying solvent, ratio, temperature and time to extract lipids from oilseed/algal meal or to partition FAME from glycerol/soap; dispense reagents, mix, heat, phase-separate, sample, quantify recovery and purity by GC/HPLC, and iterate on the results.

Bench/lab-scale recovery unit runs: recover methanol, hexane or ethanol from a reaction or extract stream by rotary evaporation, flash or fractional distillation on lab glassware or a small packed column; set up apparatus, run a temperature/vacuum profile, collect and weigh fractions, assay distillate and bottoms purity, close the mass balance and check residual product against spec.

Pilot/demonstration-scale recovery campaign at the company's pilot facility: run a skid-mounted evaporator, distillation column, decanter/centrifuge or membrane unit on tens to hundreds of liters of real process material; line up valves and hoses, charge feed, start up and hold conditions over a shift, pull grab samples for analysis, respond to foaming/fouling/upsets, shut down and clean.

Field trial at a partner's operating biodiesel/ethanol plant or feedstock site: hook a trial recovery unit or slipstream test onto as-found plant equipment, sample tanks, decanters and process lines outdoors in variable weather, log conditions over several days with plant staff, troubleshoot non-standard piping and off-spec feed, and gather data to validate lab findings at scale.

tasks.label: Count money and make bank deposits.

instances.label: Nightly close at a restaurant: manager pulls cash drawers from POS terminals, carries them to the back office, counts bills and coins by hand, reconciles totals against the POS sales/tender report, records over/short, and seals the deposit in a bag with a deposit slip.

Opening and shift-change cash handling: manager counts out starting banks/floats for each register from the safe, issues them to cashiers, and takes mid-shift cash drops from drawers, counting and logging each drop into the safe.

Bank run: manager drives the sealed deposit bag from the restaurant to a bank branch or night depository, hands it to a teller or feeds it into a drop chute/commercial ATM, and returns with the receipt (often also picking up a change order).

High-volume venue (stadium concession, catering operation, large cafeteria or hotel food service): a cash-room count of many drawers plus loose coin, checks and vouchers, using a currency counter and coin sorter, producing a multi-thousand-dollar deposit and per-stand reconciliation.

Small independent restaurant after close: owner-manager counts one or two drawers plus tip cash and customer checks at a back table or cramped office, writes a handwritten deposit slip, and holds the bag in the safe for the next day's deposit.

instances.label: Weekly or monthly full physical food inventory in a full-service restaurant: manager walks the walk-in cooler, freezer, dry storage and bar, counting sealed cases, cans and bottles, eyeballing or weighing partially used bags, tubs and unlabeled prep containers on crowded wire shelving, then keys counts into a spreadsheet or inventory app and reconciles against theoretical usage.

Daily/per-shift par-level and line checks: manager walks the kitchen line, prep area and bar during or between services, judging how much product remains in hotel pans, Cambros, kegs and open cases, noting shortages on an order guide and building the next order.

Receiving a distributor delivery at the back door/dock: check pallets and cases against the invoice, count units, probe temperatures on cold and frozen items, inspect produce and protein quality, reject or credit damaged/short items, sign the manifest, then stow stock in the cooler and dry storage with FIFO rotation and update inventory records.

Periodic equipment and smallwares inventory: count china, glassware, flatware, sheet pans, knives and serving equipment; log breakage, loss and par shortfalls; inspect condition/working order of fryers, mixers, coolers and dish machines and record items needing repair or replacement.

Institutional or multi-unit food service (school district central kitchen, hospital, campus dining, catering commissary): periodic count of a large storeroom/freezer with pallet racking and bulk cases, case-level barcode counting fed into an ERP/inventory system, plus discrepancy reporting.

instances.label: Peak-service line check in a restaurant/cafeteria kitchen: insert a probe thermometer into hot-held and cold-held foods in wells and on the line (sanitizing the probe between items), test sanitizer bucket strength with test strips, watch crew for handwashing, glove changes, bare-hand contact and ill-employee signs, correct violations on the spot, and initial the temperature log. Hot, wet, crowded line with staff moving constantly.

Opening/closing back-of-house sanitation and equipment checks: read walk-in, reach-in and freezer temperatures, verify dish machine wash/rinse temperature and final-rinse sanitizer, check hood filters and grease build-up, inspect labeling/dating and raw-over-cooked storage order inside coolers, confirm handwash sinks stocked and chemicals stored properly, and complete the written log.

Fire and life-safety walkthrough of kitchen, dining room, corridors and storage: exits and aisles unobstructed, exit signs and emergency lighting working, extinguishers mounted with charged gauges and current inspection tags, hood suppression system service tag current, sprinkler head and electrical panel clearances, combustibles stored properly; flag and clear problems found.

Building-maintenance condition round of the dining facility (and in lodging, back-of-house and public areas): check refrigeration and HVAC operation, look for water/refrigerant leaks, dripping plumbing and clogged floor drains, failed lighting, damaged flooring or ceiling tiles, and equipment running hot or noisy; log findings and issue work orders to maintenance or a contractor.

Back-office compliance records review: check the day's temperature and cleaning logs for gaps, verify hood-cleaning, ansul service, grease-trap and pest-control certificates are current, confirm food-handler cards and allergen training records, and document corrective actions before the next audit.

Health department inspection or third-party audit visit: escort the inspector through the kitchen and lodging food areas, retrieve records on request, perform immediate corrections (discard out-of-temperature food, relabel and re-date items, relocate chemicals, re-set a sanitizer bucket), then sign the report and brief staff on the correction plan.

tasks.label: Test cooked food by tasting and smelling it to ensure palatability and flavor conformity.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-shift line check in a full-service restaurant kitchen: the manager tastes and smells the day's house-made recurring items (soups, stocks, sauces, dressings, braises, sides) against fixed recipe standards before doors open, approving each or sending it back for correction. Same recipes recur daily; 30-60 minutes of lead time.

During service, the manager spot-tastes at the pass: a cook-to-order sauce, a special, a plated dish about to leave the kitchen. Dishes vary widely and include daily specials with no fixed reference; the accept/correct decision must be made in seconds while the plate is hot.

High-volume standardized production (school district central kitchen, hospital/senior-living kitchen, college dining, chain QSR or commissary): the manager samples a large kettle or pan batch of a standardized, repeatedly produced recipe before it goes on the serving line, checking seasoning and conformity to the corporate/district spec.

Menu development and vendor sampling: the manager tastes new dishes, limited-time offers, reformulated items or supplier samples, judging guest appeal and overall palatability of food with no existing reference standard, and directing recipe changes.

Suspect-batch or ingredient check: the manager smells and tastes a held batch, a product near its use-by date, or a delivered ingredient to decide whether it is off (sour, rancid, spoiled) and must be discarded or remade.

Guest complaint follow-up: a returned plated dish is brought back and the manager tastes and smells it to judge whether the complaint is valid (over/under-seasoned, off flavor, wrong preparation) and decide on a remake or comp.

It is the same sensory-check act on the same objects (cooked egg/tomato dishes) with the same output (is the seasoning right), performed by a robot arm on a lab bench, so it transfers to a manager's seasoning conformity check when the sample is presented to the machine.

sources.transferJustification: Cited only to support negative judgments about real-time tasting during service; it describes the sample-preparation and latency limits of the instruments that otherwise substantiate bench-top conformity checks.

instances.label: Casino race & sports book counter: takes a bettor's cash, enters selection/stake/odds into the wagering system, prints and hands over the paper ticket receipt; later scans a presented winning ticket and pays it out in cash. Straight bets, parlays, futures; heavy peaks on game days.

Slot floor hand-pay: a machine locks up on a taxable jackpot; manager verifies the win and machine state, checks the player's ID, completes W-2G/tax paperwork, pays the amount in cash or ticket, and obtains the player's signature.

Live table pit, routine wagering: selling chips for cash at the table, taking in losing wagers, paying winning bets in chips at the correct odds, coloring up, and recording/issuing table fills and credits during continuous play in a crowded pit.

Exception handling at tables/floor: a disputed, ambiguous or oversized payout, a suspected dealer error or device malfunction — the manager reconstructs the sequence (surveillance review if needed), rules on the bet, authorizes and pays the amount, and signs the payout slip.

Cage and keno/simulcast counter: redeeming chips and tickets for cash, writing keno or race tickets against cash, paying winning tickets, verifying ID and completing currency-transaction/AML paperwork on large cash-outs.

Off-site or temporary operation — charity casino night, tournament in a rented hall, small card room: manager collects buy-ins and wagers in cash, records them, issues receipts, and pays winners cash at the end of play; layout, equipment and crowd vary by venue.

Hosts a seated parlour-style group game for guests or residents in a lounge or day room (bingo, trivia, cards): sets out cards and prizes, calls numbers or questions, keeps the group engaged, verifies wins and helps players who fall behind.

Plans and organizes a large special event or a season of programming at a park or recreation facility: builds the schedule, books instructors/vendors/permits, walks the site to lay out stations and signage, stages tables, tents and equipment with staff, then troubleshoots the layout and flow on event day.

instances.label: Minor-injury care at an indoor recreation facility (community rec center, YMCA, water park, bowling or skating center): a patron or child presents with a scrape, blister, small laceration or bump; the manager takes the person to the office or first-aid room, dons gloves, cleans the wound, applies antiseptic and an adhesive dressing or ice pack, confirms the person is stable, and completes an incident report.

Sudden collapse of a patron (suspected cardiac arrest) on a gym floor, pool deck or theater aisle: the manager checks responsiveness and breathing, directs a bystander to call 911, positions the person, performs chest compressions and rescue breaths, retrieves and applies AED pads, follows the AED prompts, and continues until EMS arrives.

Outdoor camp, trail, ballfield or nature-park incident: a camper or participant with a twisted ankle, laceration, heat exhaustion, bee sting or fall injury, reached on foot over uneven ground; the manager assesses, controls bleeding, wraps or splints, cools and shades the person, and assists or arranges transport back to base.

Fall or attraction injury in a controlled guest area (amusement park midway, playground, waterpark deck, cruise-ship deck): bleeding wound or possible fracture; the manager applies direct pressure and dressings, immobilizes the limb, keeps the guest still and calm amid a crowd, and hands off to on-site medical staff or EMS.

Airway or allergic emergency in a facility dining hall, snack bar or activity room: a choking guest requiring back blows and abdominal thrusts, or anaphylaxis/asthma requiring the person's epinephrine auto-injector or inhaler to be administered, followed by monitoring until EMS arrives.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a dressing. It is the closest robotic analogue to first-aid bandaging, but covers only tape manipulation on static anatomical models in a lab workspace, so it does not substantiate completing a first-aid episode on a conscious, moving injured person.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue manipulation. It shows precise autonomous tissue work only on an immobilized, anesthetized, surgically exposed subject; first aid requires approaching an unfixtured conscious casualty, assessing them and selecting an intervention, none of which is demonstrated.
