tasks.label: Inspect equipment, such as rides, games, and vehicles, to detect wear and damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily pre-opening inspection round at an amusement or water park: manager/lead walks each ride, checks track and reach envelope for debris, looks over trains, wheels, cables, chains, hydraulic lines and restraints, pull-tests restraints, listens during a test cycle, and logs wear or damage before the ride opens.

Periodic in-depth inspection during downtime or off-season: ride structures, coaster track welds, towers, waterslide flumes and joints, drive motors, gearboxes and brakes examined for corrosion, cracks, fastener wear; components pulled and sent for closer examination; documented against ASTM/manufacturer checklists.

Indoor recreation/fitness center round: treadmills, ellipticals, cable and weight machines, climbing gear, spa and pool circulation equipment checked for frayed cables, worn belts and pads, cracked frames, loose fasteners, leaks; equipment run briefly to confirm function; damaged units tagged out.

Outdoor park, campground or municipal playground inspection: play structures, swings and chains, slides, sports courts, fencing and bleachers checked for wear, rust, splintering, vandalism, missing hardware and surfacing problems, in whatever weather and condition the site is found.

Vehicle and watercraft check at a maintenance shop, cart barn, marina or depot: golf carts, shuttle vans, ATVs, rental bikes, pontoon or ski boats inspected for tire wear, brake and belt condition, fluid leaks, body and hull damage before being put in service.

Arcade, midway game and family-entertainment-center equipment: game cabinets, joysticks/buttons and coin/prize mechanisms, laser-tag gear, bowling pinsetters, go-kart bodies and bumpers checked for wear, damage and correct function.

sources.title: Duos Technologies, Inc. | Automated Inspection of Rail Vehicles
sources.claim: Duos Technologies' Railcar Inspection Portal is a fixed, purpose-built machine-vision/AI portal that rolling stock passes through at track speed; the system automatically images and analyzes hundreds of components to detect mechanical defects and damage, and is in commercial operation on North American railroads.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated inspection of rail vehicles for mechanical wear and damage. It transfers to inspecting amusement ride trains, karts and fleet vehicles because the objects are comparable steel running gear (wheels, axles, brakes, springs, linkages), the defect classes are the same (wear, cracks, missing/loose hardware), and the work is presented to a fixed portal exactly as a purpose-built cell would present it.

sources.title: Supply Side: Cando/Caltrax; Duos; Railroad Software; Siemens Mobility - Railway Age
sources.claim: Thirteen RIP portals were reported in operation with four major ..., performing millions of automated scans to detect and identify railcar ....
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (automated rail vehicle condition inspection); establishes commercial deployment scale and that the output is accepted in place of manual inspection.

sources.system: UVeye Helios / Artemis / Atlas drive-through inspection systems
sources.title: UVeye Expands AI-Powered Vehicle Inspections to Trucks, Buses, and Commercial Fleets
sources.claim: UVeye's automated drive-through inspection systems scan vehicles and automatically report tire wear, underbody leaks, cracks and rust, and exterior damage; they are installed at hundreds of dealerships and at fleet, rental and logistics operators, and have been extended to trucks and buses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated vehicle condition inspection at fleet and rental operations. It transfers to a recreation manager's cart/van/ATV check because the detected conditions (tire wear, brake/underbody wear, fluid leaks, body damage) are the same items on the manager's checklist, with the vehicle presented to a fixed purpose-built scanning station.

sources.system: Robotic machine-vision inspection cell (UR robot arm with 3D scanners)
sources.title: Machine Vision | Adams Corp
sources.claim: Deployed robotic inspection cells use a robot arm carrying 3D scanners to position sensors and automatically detect surface and dimensional defects on presented parts, replacing manual visual inspection on a production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated defect/wear inspection of fixtured mechanical parts. It transfers to inspecting ride components, playground hardware and gym-machine parts brought to a purpose-built station, because the objects are similar metal assemblies and the defect classes (cracks, surface wear, damage) and required precision are comparable or tighter.

sources.system: ML-powered robotic vision inspection (survey of >50 deployed/studied systems)
sources.title: Machine Learning-Powered Vision for Robotic Inspection in Manufacturing: A Review
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed 2026 review finds machine-learning vision for robotic inspection is technically viable and in use across automotive, aerospace and general manufacturing for automated defect detection and classification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic visual defect detection on fixtured workpieces; establishes that automated wear/damage detection at a purpose-built station is a mature, broadly deployed capability rather than a one-off demo.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Orbit software
sources.title: Orbit 5.0 adds features to Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds inside industrial facilities — navigating a 40-acre plant, docking to recharge, and capturing thermal, acoustic and gauge data — and Orbit 5.0 automatically flags visual anomalies such as corrosion, debris and spills without manual image review.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-situ equipment inspection rounds in a structured facility. It shows the current E2 envelope is fixed-route sensing of instrumented plant assets (thermal/acoustic/gauge/corrosion), not the hands-on functional checks (restraint pull tests, brake and belt feel, test cycling) that ride, gym and playground inspections require.

sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas Leaks | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: A midstream plant deployed Spot for autonomous inspection applications including anomaly ... inspection and gauge reading, navigating a 40-acre facility and recharging between rounds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous facility inspection rounds; cited to characterize what mobile robots do achieve at E2 (industrial plants with pre-configured action points) versus recreation equipment inspection.

sources.system: Flyability Elios drone (INTECH NDE inspection of West Edmonton Mall water rides and Mindbender coaster)
sources.title: Elios Drone Revolutionizes Amusement Park Inspections
sources.claim: Drone inspection of amusement rides at a park is performed by a certified human pilot flying the aircraft, not by an autonomous system, and covers only visual access to hard-to-reach structure.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (amusement ride inspection); cited as a negative datum showing that in-park ride inspection today is pilot-controlled, so it cannot support an autonomous E2 judgment.

tasks.label: Clean equipment and areas of amusement park, cruise ship, or other recreational facility.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hard-floor cleaning of large indoor public areas of the facility — arena/water-park concourses, bowling center and skating-rink lobbies, arcade floors, cruise-ship atriums and public decks: sweeping, scrubbing and vacuuming open floor, usually before opening or overnight, with spot attention to spills and sticky residue.

Outdoor grounds of the facility — midways, walkways, plazas, picnic lawns and campground/sports-complex grounds: sweeping paved areas and picking up scattered litter (cups, wrappers, cigarette butts, popcorn) during or after operating hours, around guests and fixed furniture.
Guest restrooms and locker rooms: cleaning and disinfecting toilets, urinals and sinks, mopping/scrubbing floors, clearing trash, in high-traffic public washrooms of the recreational facility.

Pool, splash pad, spa or water feature: vacuuming the floor and walls, brushing the waterline, and skimming debris in a commercial swimming pool or water-park basin so it meets health-code clarity before opening.

In-place wipe-down and sanitizing of high-touch recreation equipment fixed in the venue — arcade/game cabinets, fitness machines, ride restraint bars and seats, party-room tables, handrails — using cloth and disinfectant on varied, delicate, electronics-bearing surfaces.

Washing removable gear and ride/rental vehicles in a maintenance area — go-karts, bumper boats, kayaks, golf carts, rental helmets and skates, pool furniture — hosed, scrubbed, sanitized and set out to dry.

tasks.label: Operate, drive, or explain the use of mechanical equipment in amusement parks, cruise ships, or other recreational facilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Driving a cart, shuttle, or electric vehicle on paved routes inside resort/park grounds — moving guests, staff, or supplies between hotel, midway, pool, and back-of-house areas, among pedestrians, on premises the operator controls.

Driving a pickup, van, or UTV around and beyond the facility — public streets, gravel service roads, campground loops and unimproved trails — hauling gear, towing a trailer of chairs/kayaks, checking remote sites.

Explaining and hands-on demonstrating equipment to guests and training staff: how to work the ride control panel and e-stop, fit a climbing harness, paddle a rental kayak, use the fitness machines or bowling equipment; answering questions and correcting mistakes.

Operating ride/attraction equipment during peak or break coverage: loading and unloading guests, verifying restraints and loose articles, dispatching from the control panel, monitoring the cycle, restarting after an e-stop; also running a chairlift or waterslide dispatch.

Operating grounds and facility machinery: mowing turf and ballfields, running the ice resurfacer between sessions, pool vacuum/filtration systems, line marking, and a lift truck to move staging and event equipment.
Operating watercraft at a waterfront facility: pontoon/ski boat, rental fleet launch, tender or dock maneuvers with guests aboard on a lake, river, or harbor.

tasks.label: Inspect guest rooms, public areas, and grounds for cleanliness and appearance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-housekeeping spot-check of a vacant, cleaned guest room in a limited- or full-service hotel: manager walks the room, checks bed making and linen appearance, bathroom (tub, toilet, mirror, grout, hair/water spots), dusting of surfaces and ledges, vacuumed carpet, emptied trash, correctly stocked and aligned amenities; releases the room or returns it to the attendant.

Indoor public-area walkthrough during operating hours with guests and staff present: lobby, corridors, elevators, public restrooms, breakfast/bar area, fitness room and indoor pool deck; looking for litter, spills, smudged glass, dusty ledges, overflowing bins, disarranged furniture, missing supplies, and general appearance against brand standards.

Exterior grounds and curb-appeal walk: entry drive, porte-cochere, parking lot, sidewalks, landscaping beds, signage, exterior lighting, patio/pool furniture, dumpster enclosure; noting litter, cigarette butts, weeds, stains, seasonal debris or snow, and damaged or dirty exterior surfaces, in varying weather and light.

Formal brand-standard or QA audit of a sample of rooms with a scored checklist and photo documentation: deeper checks under beds and behind headboards, inside drawers, closets and minibar, high ledges and vents (white-glove), linen and upholstery condition, with a written score and deficiency list submitted to the brand or ownership.

Inspection triggered by a guest complaint or a VIP/occupied room: entering a room in use with the guest's belongings scattered, or a room reported as dirty, malodorous or pest-affected; assessing the condition, often with the guest present, and directing immediate remediation or a room move.

sources.system: Porsche Leipzig automated paint defect detection system (robot-mounted scanning sensors + AI)
sources.title: Porsche Automates Paint Inspection with AI-Powered Robotic System
sources.claim: Robot arms with sensors automatically scan every painted car body at Porsche's Leipzig plant and an AI system detects and locates dust particles, debris inclusions and other surface defects in a fixed inspection station, replacing subjective manual visual inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated visual inspection of large finished surfaces for contamination and appearance defects. It transfers to inspecting room surfaces for dust, debris and stains because the perceptual problem (finding small particles and blemishes on finished surfaces and grading them against a standard) and the accepted output (a located, classified deficiency list handed to staff for rework) are comparable, in a purpose-built fixtured station where the workpiece is presented in a known position under controlled lighting.

sources.title: CarPaintVision — ISRA VISION

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-carried visual inspection of complete large surfaces with defect classification against customer-specific standards, analogous to grading a presented workpiece against hotel brand cleanliness standards. Transfer holds only where the item is fixtured and presented, as in a purpose-built inspection cell.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places

It shows the mobility and reporting half of a walkthrough is solved at E2, but the detections are security, access and environmental events, not cleanliness or appearance grading, so it does not substantiate completion of this task at E2.

It covers only the floor-litter fraction of a public-area inspection and produces cleaning, not an inspection report on fixtures, glass, furniture, restrooms and stocking, so it does not substantiate completion of the instance at E2.

sources.title: Angsa Robotics Uses Swift to Increase Efficiency of Autonomous Trash Picking Robots

instances.label: Environment-of-care/safety round on a hospital patient care unit or clinic clinical area: manager walks the unit with a checklist, checks corridor egress clearance and clutter, sharps containers, secured oxygen cylinders, medication and supply storage (locks, expiration dates, refrigerator temps), cleanliness/infection-control conditions, ceiling tiles and penetrations, opens cabinets and doors, questions staff, then logs deficiencies and recommends fixes or equipment changes.

Emergency-readiness / life-safety inspection of the facility: verifying fire extinguishers are present, charged and tagged, exit signs and emergency lighting work (press-to-test), fire doors latch and are unobstructed, pull stations and sprinkler clearances, emergency power outlets and generator area, disaster/evacuation supplies and posted routes; writing up deficiencies and recommending building or equipment modifications.

Access/ADA and public-area walkthrough of an outpatient clinic or hospital public zone with facilities staff: entrance and ramp slopes, door widths and opening force, accessible restroom grab bars and clearances, counter and signage heights, accessible parking and path of travel, waiting-room layout; measuring conditions and recommending building modifications or renovation work.

Rounds of mechanical, utility and support spaces (boiler/chiller and electrical rooms, storage rooms, soiled/clean utility, waste and biohazard storage, loading dock): checking equipment condition and gauges, leaks, overheating, ventilation, blocked exits and housekeeping on a repeatable route, and flagging items for repair or equipment upgrade.

Sanitation-focused inspection of food service, laundry, sterile processing or environmental-services performance: dish machine and sanitizer checks, food and cooler temperatures with a probe, food-contact surfaces and floor drains, sterilizer logs and instrument handling, cleaning quality audit of rooms; documenting violations and recommending equipment replacement or process changes.

Inspection of an active renovation or construction zone in or adjacent to the operating facility (ICRA/ILSM rounds): verifying dust barriers and anteroom integrity, negative-pressure readings, temporary egress and fire-watch arrangements, debris and contractor practices in an unfinished, changing space; directing corrections and recommending modifications.

instances.label: Scheduled outpatient study visit at a research site: coordinator seats the subject, applies the protocol-specified cuff after a timed rest, records blood pressure, pulse, respiratory rate, temperature plus weight/height, and enters values into source documents/eCRF. Ambulatory adult subjects, standard exam room.

Protocol-timepoint 12-lead ECG at the research clinic: subject undressed to the waist and positioned supine, skin prepped (occasionally shaved), 10 electrodes located by anatomical landmarks and adhered, tracing acquired, checked for artifact, printed/uploaded and screened for clinically significant abnormalities.

Face-to-face administration of a fixed-script instrument at a clinic visit (symptom scale, quality-of-life or pain questionnaire, diary review) where the coordinator reads standardized items and records the subject's chosen responses verbatim.

Open-ended protocol interviewing at a clinic visit: eligibility and medical-history questioning, adverse-event elicitation with follow-up probing on onset/severity/causality, concomitant-medication and compliance review, and contemporaneous source documentation of the narrative.

Phase I inpatient unit intensive PK/PD day: serial vital signs and serial 12-lead ECGs on multiple subjects at exact clocked timepoints (predose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 h), subjects semi-recumbent in beds with IV lines, tight time windows.

Off-site visit at a subject's home, nursing home, or community/mobile site: coordinator carries equipment into a room taken as found, takes vitals and asks protocol symptom/AE questions, sometimes with a mobile ECG unit.

instances.label: Post-visit specimen processing in the site's small processing room/lab: coordinator receives freshly drawn protocol tubes, applies protocol-specific labels, inverts/holds for clotting per lab manual, centrifuges at specified g/time, pipettes serum/plasma into pre-labeled cryovials, logs volumes and times in the lab requisition/eCRF, and places aliquots in the -20/-80 freezer box position recorded in the inventory.

Preparing and sending a shipment to the central lab: pulling the correct aliquots from the freezer per the shipping manifest, packing them in the sponsor's insulated shipper with absorbent and secondary containment plus dry ice or ambient packs, completing the requisition/manifest and airway bill, applying UN3373/dry-ice markings, and handing off to the scheduled courier within the protocol window.

Requisition and kit readiness: ordering study lab kits and supplies, receiving and stocking them, checking kit contents and expiry dates, and assembling the visit-specific kit (correct tube types in draw order, cryovials, protocol labels, requisition forms) laid out on the bench before the participant visit.

Specimen collection at the participant visit in a clinic exam or draw room: verifying subject ID against labels, performing or directly overseeing venipuncture into the protocol tube set in the required order of draw and fill volumes, and recording collection times; occasional urine/saliva/swab collection.

Storage management: daily/weekly freezer and refrigerator temperature checks and logs, responding to temperature alarms and moving boxes to a backup unit, periodic inventory reconciliation of stored specimens against the study log, and retrieving specimens for shipment, retest, or destruction at study close.

Moving time-critical specimens within the institution: hand-carrying or arranging transport of tubes, cytology/pathology containers, or fresh tissue from clinic, OR, or ward to the hospital core lab, pathology, or the site's processing lab within protocol stability windows, with chain-of-custody sign-off at drop-off.

instances.label: Study start-up at a clinic/academic research site: the coordinator claims a lockable cabinet or storeroom shelf bay, unpacks sponsor shipments (lab kit cartons, source binders, tubes, shipping containers, IATA supplies), sorts contents by protocol and visit, arranges them into labeled bins/shelves, and logs inventory.

Routine replenishment and tidying of study supplies in exam/procedure rooms and phlebotomy carts: restocking tubes, needles, kits, requisitions and PPE into designated drawers, bins and cart trays; rotating stock so nearest-expiry items are in front; discarding out-of-date items.

Arranging study equipment in the research space: siting and positioning a centrifuge, refrigerator/freezer, ECG machine, scale, spirometer or dedicated workstation; clearing bench/floor space, connecting power and data, routing cables, placing temperature probes and ensuring staff access.

Organizing investigational product / temperature-controlled storage: arranging drug kits in a locked, temperature-monitored cabinet or refrigerator by kit number, lot and expiry; segregating by protocol and quarantining expired or returned product for accountability.

Planning the space itself: walking the site, measuring the room, deciding what goes where, negotiating with clinic managers/facilities and the sponsor monitor for lockable and monitored space, ordering shelving/refrigerators and coordinating their installation.

Periodic purge, study closeout or protocol amendment cleanup: pulling expired/obsolete supplies and superseded materials, boxing documents and remaining kits for sponsor return or archive, and re-laying-out the remaining stock in the freed space.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine monitoring run on a utility-managed reservoir or lake: boat/USV visits a set of fixed stations, records temperature, pH, DO, conductivity, turbidity and chlorophyll-a with a multiparameter sonde, and collects surface/depth grab bottles for lab analysis; access controlled by the utility.

Roving field run to several small streams, creeks and river bridge/bank sites: park roadside, walk or wade to the site, take field parameters, fill and preserve grab bottles (nutrients, metals, bacteria), record observations and chain of custody; sites taken as found (vegetation, mud banks, variable flow).

Permit compliance sampling inside a wastewater or drinking-water treatment plant: program and service the flow-paced automatic composite sampler at influent/effluent, pull scheduled grabs at process points and taps, preserve, log chain of custody, verify continuous online analyzers.

Biological monitoring in a wadeable stream: kick-net macroinvertebrate collection from riffles, periphyton/algae scrapes, habitat assessment, occasional electrofishing pass; heavy wading over cobble in variable flow.

Groundwater monitoring-well round at a landfill, industrial site or wellfield: open the well, measure depth to water, purge with a bladder/submersible pump using low-flow criteria until field parameters stabilize, then fill and preserve bottles for the compliance suite.

Servicing and calibrating continuous monitoring instrumentation at fixed gauge stations/buoys (sonde swaps, cleaning, calibration, data verification) and overseeing crews/contractors in the field: QA audits of technique, collecting split/duplicate QC samples alongside them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine issuance at the retail window of a mid-size post office: a walk-in customer asks for one domestic money order (typically $50-$500) and pays cash; the postmaster/supervisor covering the window keys the amount into the retail terminal, the money order imprinter prints it, cash and fee are collected, change counted out, and the money order plus receipt handed to the customer.

Cashing a presented money order at the window: customer presents a completed USPS money order (usually under $500), the postmaster inspects it for authenticity and alteration (watermark, security thread, amount imprint), confirms endorsement and checks photo ID when required, then counts out currency from the drawer, subject to office cash on hand.

Bank Secrecy Act-sensitive sale: a customer buys multiple money orders or $3,000+ in money orders with cash in one day; the postmaster must inspect and record photo identification on the funds-transaction report (PS Form 8105-A), watch for structuring or suspicious behavior, and complete or refuse the sale accordingly.

Money order line item inside a busy mixed window transaction at a high-volume office during peak hours: the customer also mails a parcel or buys stamps, may need help filling in payee/purchaser fields, may pay by debit card, and the queue must keep moving.

Exception handling at the window in a small or rural office: a spoiled/misprinted money order must be voided and reissued, an unused money order refunded to its purchaser, or a lost/stolen money order inquiry taken (PS Form 6401 with fee), with the accountable blank money order stock secured and the day's money order report reconciled.

instances.label: Routine floor cleaning of interior common areas at a mid-size or large managed multifamily/commercial property: vacuuming carpeted corridors and community rooms, sweeping and mopping the lobby and elevator-lobby hard floors on a repeated route, layout fixed and controlled by management.

Detail tidy of common areas: emptying and relining trash cans, wiping glass entry doors and handrails, cleaning elevator interiors, sweeping stairwells and landings, tidying the mail and laundry rooms, spot-cleaning spills, restocking a common restroom.

Changing burned-out light bulbs and tubes: ladder access to corridor ceiling fixtures, exterior wall packs and parking-lot lamps, and fixtures inside units; removing a globe or diffuser, swapping the lamp, restoring the fixture and verifying it lights.

Minor repairs inside occupied or vacant dwelling units: dripping faucet or cartridge, running toilet, sticking door or lockset, loose cabinet hinge, patching nail holes and touch-up paint, replacing an outlet cover, plunging or snaking a slow drain.

Minor repairs in common areas and on the exterior: tightening a loose handrail bracket, adjusting a door closer, fixing a gate latch or mailbox door, re-caulking a joint, replacing a broken floor tile, securing loose trim or a fence board.
Exterior grounds cleaning on the property: sweeping or blowing paved walkways, entry aprons and parking areas, clearing leaves and litter from hard surfaces and around the dumpster enclosure.

sources.title: Avidbots Designs Fully Autonomous Cleaning Robots for Airports and Hospitals
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo is a fully ... deployed in large human-occupied commercial facilities (airports, malls, hospitals, schools), i.e. structured facilities kept to a working standard.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (cleaning floors of common areas of a building); the workpiece (lobby/corridor floors) and quality standard match the property manager's routine floor cleaning.

sources.title: Avidbots releases floor-scrubbing robot for industrial spaces
sources.claim: Avidbots reports more than 1,000 autonomous floor-scrubbing robots in the field cleaning businesses, airports, schools and warehouses, indicating routine at-scale deployment rather than a demo.

sources.title: Whiz - ROBOTS: Your Guide to the World of Robotics

sources.transferJustification: Same task (vacuuming carpeted common corridors); hotel corridors are functionally identical to apartment/condo corridors in layout, floor type and cleanliness standard.

sources.title: The Robotics Founder Who Turned a Hotel Chore Into a Real-World AI Breakthrough
sources.claim: Peanut Robotics fields a commercially deployed mobile manipulator that autonomously cleans hotel bathrooms (wiping surfaces with a cloth in mapped, static rooms), but its scope is restroom surfaces, not bin emptying, glass entries or stairwells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (hotel bathroom cleaning) shows surface-wiping manipulation in a structured facility, but it is confined to mapped restrooms and does not cover trash, glass doors, or stairwells.

sources.title: Toilet-cleaning robot makes us feel better about all this AI business

sources.title: Gausium Launches WeatherSense Guard: Bringing Intelligent Weather Awareness to the Beetle Outdoor Sweeper

sources.title: Angsa Robotics Uses Swift to Increase Efficiency of Autonomous Trash Picking Robots

sources.title: Five examples of automated industrial systems crafted by Universal Robots

instances.label: Routine grounds walk of a multifamily apartment community or HOA: parking lots and drive aisles, sidewalks, landscaping and irrigation, trash enclosures, pool/playground, exterior lighting and building exteriors; the manager notes trip hazards, potholes, litter/dumping, broken fixtures, burned-out lights, damaged fencing and gates, and writes a maintenance punch list. Residents, cars, kids and pets are present; terrain includes curbs, grass and stairs.

Weekly/monthly walk-through of interior common areas of a commercial office building or condo high-rise: lobby, corridors, stairwells, restrooms, elevators, laundry/amenity rooms and parking garage; checking lighting, ceiling stains and water leaks, damaged finishes and doors, cleanliness, and life-safety signage; issues logged as work orders.

Routine check of building equipment and mechanical spaces: boiler/mechanical rooms, rooftop HVAC units, pumps, electrical panels, elevator machine room, sprinkler riser and generator; reading gauges and meters, listening for abnormal noise, spotting leaks/puddles, checking belts and filters, logging readings and flagging service needs to vendors.

Roof and building-envelope/exterior structure inspection, including after storms: roof membrane or shingles, flashing, gutters and downspouts, facade and stucco/siding, parking deck and site drainage; access by ladder or roof hatch, as-found conditions with debris, ponding and weather exposure; output is a damage/repair determination and photos for a contractor or insurance claim.

Interior inspection of individual dwelling units (move-in/move-out, annual unit inspection, scattered single-family rentals): occupied or vacant unit with furniture and personal belongings; checking under sinks for leaks, appliances, water heater, walls/floors/finishes, windows, smoke detectors and HVAC filters; documenting condition and repair needs room by room.

sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs automated inspection missions in industrial facilities including thermal monitoring, acoustic leak detection ... analog gauge reading, planned and managed through Orbit software, with an arm that opens doors on autonomous missions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine equipment rounds in plant mechanical spaces. Same objects (gauges, pumps, piping, panels), same output (readings plus a flag that maintenance is needed) as a property manager's boiler-room/rooftop-unit check.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics and Google DeepMind Unveil a Smarter Spot - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Several thousand Spot robots are commercially deployed doing inspection work, and Spot now runs Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics-ER embodied reasoning model for inspection tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes fleet-scale, non-demo deployment of the inspection platform relied on for equipment and facility rounds.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics Spot uses DeepMind for machinery inspections
sources.claim: The Gemini-equipped Spot autonomously inspects assets for conveyor damage, sight-glass levels and gauge readings, identifies standing liquid puddles and performs housekeeping (5S) audits that previously took multiple people across shifts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated facility condition/housekeeping walkthroughs. Detecting damage, spills and out-of-standard conditions on a fixed route is the same perceptual judgment a manager makes on a common-area or mechanical-room walk.

instances.label: Periodic readiness walkthrough of the primary and alternate emergency operations center in a city/county government building or hospital command center: confirm that workstations, monitors, video wall, phones, desk radios, printers/plotters, maps, plan binders, and consumable supplies are present, in place, undamaged, and powered; note clutter, damage, or missing items on a checklist and write up deficiencies. Fixed, familiar, badge-controlled site.

Functional check of communications equipment: monthly/quarterly radio checks with field units, neighboring jurisdictions and the state on VHF/UHF/700-800 MHz talkgroups; satellite phone and HF tests; test transmissions through repeaters; test of the mass-notification/alerting system; verification that the mobile command vehicle's onboard radios, mast, and consoles work. Involves keying radios, judging audio quality and coverage, coordinating with remote stations, and troubleshooting.

Inspection of backup power and building support systems serving the EOC, 911 center, or other critical facility: generator condition, fuel level and gauges, coolant/oil sight glasses, start batteries, automatic transfer switch and UPS status panels, HVAC and cooling for equipment rooms; observing a scheduled exercise run and noting hot spots, leaks, or alarm conditions. Fixed generator rooms and fenced generator yards at an institution-controlled facility.

Pre-designation survey or periodic re-inspection of shelters and alternate facilities (schools, churches, community centers, fairgrounds): measure usable floor area, check ADA access routes and restrooms/showers, kitchen equipment, generator hookups and panel capacity, roof and structural condition, hazards and egress; assess against Red Cross/state shelter criteria and complete a survey form. Layouts differ site to site; the inspector visits buildings that are unfamiliar and not prepared for the visit.

Inspection of equipment caches and mobile assets in a county warehouse, apparatus bay, or storage trailers: count and verify stocked items (cots, blankets, water, MREs, PPE, sandbags), check expiration dates and packaging condition, check tires, batteries and fluids on trailers and response vehicles, and start portable generators, light towers, and pumps to confirm they run under load.

Inspection of remote and outdoor infrastructure: outdoor warning siren sites, radio repeater/tower sites on hilltops or rooftops, and remote weather/stream gauges — check pole/tower and antenna condition, solar panels, battery cabinets, grounding, and confirm the unit responds when polled or activated.

sources.title: See Your Facility Like Never Before | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot with Orbit 5.0 autonomously patrols a facility, captures images at pre-set points of interest, and an AI vision-language model returns yes/no, numeric, or descriptive answers, flagging issues such as spills or a missing fire extinguisher — i.e., presence/condition checklist inspection without a human walking the route.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is routine industrial facility inspection rounds. Transfer to an EOC readiness walkthrough is close: both are indoor, pre-mapped, institution-controlled buildings; both check that fixed equipment at known locations is present, undamaged and in normal state; neither requires manipulation or fine precision.

sources.title: Orbit 5.0 adds features to Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped robot - The Robot Report

sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: automated detection of changed/missing/damaged items on a repeated route is the core of a facility readiness walkthrough.

sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot is deployed at scale for routine asset inspection in power generation and industrial facilities, having autonomously inspected over 130,000 industrial assets, with named utility deployments (National Grid substation, Dominion Energy, J-POWER geothermal plant, bp offshore rig reading gauges and listening for ...).
sources.transferJustification: Related task is utility/plant equipment inspection rounds. Backup-power inspection at an EOC involves the same object classes (generators, switchgear, pumps, gauges, panels) in fixed equipment rooms of an institution-controlled facility.

sources.title: Thermal Sensing & Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot performs scheduled autonomous thermal inspection rounds with radiometric imaging, alarm thresholds and trending for condition monitoring of electrical and mechanical equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is predictive-maintenance thermal rounds; a backup-generator/switchgear readiness check uses the same measurements (hot spots, gauge values, abnormal noise) on the same equipment types in a fixed room.

sources.title: The Next Step in Safe, Autonomous Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' 2025 release added autonomous thermal monitoring, acoustic leak detection ... to scheduled missions, and for the first time allowed the Spot Arm to open ... — establishing the limited manipulation available in autonomous inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Bounds the manipulation available in autonomous inspection missions (door opening only), which is why instances requiring operating radios, starting engines, or opening and rummaging through supply cabinets are not supported.

sources.transferJustification: Related task is warehouse inventory auditing; it covers only the counting sub-step of a cache inspection and does not extend to checking expiration dates, packaging damage, or starting trailers and generators, so it cannot substantiate the whole instance.

Item-level inventory and readiness maintenance of serialized instruments in a cache room or storage trailer (radiation pagers, electronic dosimeters, four-gas meters, PIDs, isotope identifiers): open cases, match serial numbers, check battery state and calibration due dates, run bump tests/check-source verifications, charge and update units, tag out failures and log results.

Kitting and issue at the EM warehouse/dock: pull the requested detectors, dosimeters and PPE for a fire department, bomb squad or hospital, assemble kits on carts/pallets, stage them at the dock and load them onto the receiving agency's vehicle with a signed transfer record.

Delivering equipment out to partner agencies across the jurisdiction: load a van or pickup, drive public roads, unload cases at fire stations, hospitals, schools or a regional team's quarters, carry gear inside and hand it over with paperwork.

Providing hands-on instruction to responders in the operation and maintenance of the issued equipment: demonstrating start-up and field checks, donning/doffing and decon procedures, sensor and battery care, watching trainees practice, correcting technique and answering questions.

Incident or full-scale exercise: pulling detection gear and dosimeters from the cache on short notice and distributing them to teams at a field staging area or incident command post, tracking who received what under time pressure and outdoor conditions.

instances.label: Routine walk-through inspection of the cardio and strength floor at a health club, campus rec center, or corporate fitness center: start and run treadmills/ellipticals/bikes to check belts, consoles and noise; inspect cables, pulleys, pins, upholstery and bolts on selectable-weight machines; check functional-training rigs, mats and dumbbells; tag out defective units and log findings in the preventive-maintenance record.

Hands-on minor maintenance and adjustment performed by the coordinator on varied equipment brands: lubricating treadmill decks, tightening loose hardware, re-tensioning or replacing a frayed cable, replacing worn pads/grips/pins, calibrating or rebooting consoles, changing batteries and heart-rate contacts, clearing debris from motor compartments.

Arranging outside service: diagnosing symptoms well enough to describe them, submitting work orders or calling the service contractor/manufacturer under warranty, scheduling the visit around class and peak hours, escorting and supervising the technician on the floor, verifying the repair, approving invoices and updating asset records.

Cleaning and sanitizing equipment and touchpoints during and after operating hours: wiping down machine handles, seats, consoles, benches and rigs; disinfecting mats and small equipment; re-racking dumbbells and plates; restocking wipe/spray stations and towels.

Floor care of the facility's open areas — group-exercise studio, gym/court floor, stretching area, corridors and lobby — scrubbing, mopping, vacuuming or dust-mopping hard and rubber flooring between classes or overnight in an institution-controlled building.

Larger periodic facility projects: receiving and placing new equipment, rearranging the floor layout, moving benches/racks for events or deep cleaning, reporting lighting/HVAC/mirror/locker problems to building services and coordinating vendor renovations.

instances.label: Day-spa/resort-spa manager's hygiene walk-through of treatment rooms and stations during operating hours: confirming implements were disinfected or single-use items discarded, linens and table paper changed between clients, wax pots/foot basins/hot-stone units cleaned per protocol, product jars covered, sharps and biohazard containers correct, hand-wash and sanitizer supplies stocked. Requires opening drawers/cabinets, close-up judgment of soil and residue, and immediate correction with the practitioner.

Observing staff during service delivery and client handling for protocol compliance: hand hygiene and glove use, draping and client privacy, no double-dipping of applicators, correct contraindication screening and intake, safe use of hot/electrical devices (steamers, microdermabrasion, LED, hot towels). Manager watches discreetly in occupied, semi-private rooms and coaches or corrects on the spot.

Wet-area water chemistry compliance: measuring and recording sanitizer residual, pH, and temperature for pools, whirlpools/hydrotherapy tubs and cold plunges at code-required intervals, comparing to required ranges, ordering shock/closure when out of range, and maintaining the health-department log.

Wet-area and locker-room condition check: sauna/steam room temperature and cleanliness, tub disinfection between users, drain covers and safety equipment in place, water clarity, slip hazards and standing water on decks, mildew, foot-traffic hygiene. Wet, humid, partly occupied spaces with undressed guests.

Public-area safety and hazard round of lobby, corridors, relaxation lounge and retail area: spills and wet floors, obstructions and blocked exits, cords, damaged flooring, signage, first-aid and AED availability; flagging hazards and confirming they are cleared.

Records and readiness audit: reviewing sanitation and autoclave/spore-test logs, technician licenses and certifications, SDS binder, laundry handling, labeling and secure storage of disinfectants and treatment chemicals; corrective-action follow-up and preparation for state board or health-department inspection.

tasks.label: Check spa equipment to ensure proper functioning.

instances.label: Opening/closing walkthrough of the wet area of a hotel or day spa: step into the dry sauna (80-95°C) to confirm the heater has brought it to temperature and stones/benches are sound, check the steam room (near 100% RH) is generating steam and the eucalyptus feed works, confirm whirlpool/hot tub temperature by feel and gauge, run the jets and blower, look for leaks, drips, loose fittings and cloudy water, verify lighting and emergency call buttons.

Pool/spa plant room round: confirm circulation pumps and heaters are running, read filter pressure gauges and flow meters, listen/feel for bearing or seal trouble, check for leaks around pumps and pipework, verify the chemical feed pumps and controller are operating, and test water chemistry (pH, sanitizer) against the controller's reading.

Treatment room equipment check before service: raise/lower hydraulic and electric massage tables, verify hot towel cabbies and stone warmers reach set temperature, check wax heaters, facial steamers (steam output, water level), hydrotherapy/Vichy tubs (jets, drains, hoses), and magnifying lamps across 6-12 individually laid-out rooms.

Aesthetic/medical device check: power up laser/IPL, microdermabrasion, RF or LED units, run the device's start-up self-test, confirm handpiece output and cooling, check consumables and filters, confirm calibration/service dates and record the check in the equipment log.

Responding to a mid-shift malfunction report from a therapist or guest: go to the equipment, reproduce the fault, diagnose it (tripped breaker, clogged jet, blown lamp, low water, error code), make the minor fix if possible, otherwise tag the equipment out of service and call the vendor/engineering.

sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Across the Spot fleet, navigation and data collection on inspection missions are autonomous, while arm manipulation (picking objects, opening doors) was overwhelmingly done by operators driving the robot manually.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the autonomy boundary: autonomous sensing rounds are routine, but physically operating equipment controls with the arm remains operator-driven, which bears on treatment-room device checks.

sources.system: Spot with Spot CAM+IR, MUVE C360, Enhanced Autonomy Payload
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot performs autonomous gauge reading, thermal inspection and anomaly detection on a full processing plant, docking and recharging between routes.
sources.transferJustification: Gauge reading and thermal checks are precisely the plant-room sub-checks a spa manager performs on filter pressure, flow meters and pump/motor temperature.

sources.title: ANYmal X — The World's First Ex-Proof Legged Robot
sources.claim: ANYmal (IP67-rated legged inspection robot) performs autonomous rounds reading analog gauges, liquid levels and lever positions plus thermography and vibration analysis of pumps, valves and heat exchangers in industrial plants.
sources.transferJustification: Same inspection primitives as a spa plant-room round (read gauges, confirm pumps/heaters running, spot abnormal heat or vibration) in a wet, chemically loaded, institution-controlled facility.

sources.title: ANYmal deployed at Northern Lights CCS Facility
sources.claim: ANYmal was deployed at Equinor's Northern Lights facility and ran autonomous inspection missions without local human supervision within two weeks.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms limited-intervention operation of the inspection-round capability relied on for the plant-room instance.

sources.system: Lynx M20 water utility inspection solution
sources.title: DEEP Robotics Launches Water Utility Inspection Solution
sources.claim: A quadruped inspection product aimed at water utilities patrols water tanks, chemical dosing rooms and control rooms, including recognizing instrument/knob states.
sources.transferJustification: Water-treatment plant rooms are the closest analogue to a pool/spa plant room; cited as corroboration only, autonomy of the deployment is not established.

sources.title: Commercial Swimming Pool Chemical Controllers from Recreonics
sources.claim: Commercial chemical controllers continuously measure sanitizer/pH in pool and spa water and drive dosing pumps automatically, replacing manual test-and-adjust rounds.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the water-chemistry portion of the plant-room instance: an installed machine performs the measurement and corrective dosing that the manager would otherwise do by hand.

sources.title: End-of-line testing systems for heat exchanger production | ZELTWANGER
sources.claim: End-of-line test systems built as robot cells or automated stations perform leak detection, comprehensive functional performance tests and electrical functionality/safety verification on heat-exchanger and thermal products with automatic pass/fail results.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line functional verification of heating/fluid equipment. It is the purpose-built-cell form of 'check this heater, pump or plumbing works and does not leak' — same equipment class, higher precision, fixtured presentation.

sources.system: Hänchen end-of-line test stand for hydraulic products
sources.title: End of Line test stand for hydraulic products | EoL test stand
sources.claim: A fully automatic, software-controlled end-of-line test stand carries out final functional inspection of hydraulic cylinders, pressure ... similar fluid-power products.
sources.transferJustification: Hydraulic/electric massage tables and hydrotherapy tubs are fluid-power and actuator equipment; a fixtured stand that strokes and measures them is the E1 form of the manager's 'does it lift and hold' check.

sources.title: MATT the Smart Device Test Automation Robot | Adapta Robotics
sources.claim: MATT is a commercial delta-robot test cell that physically presses buttons and touchscreens on a fixtured device, senses the device's response with cameras and microphones, and runs unattended functional test cycles for over 72 hours.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: functional check of a control-panel device. Powering up an IPL/laser or facial steamer, working its panel and confirming it responds correctly is the same interaction class on comparably sized fixtured equipment.

sources.title: Spot Information for Use v1.1, Boston Dynamics, Inc.
sources.claim: Spot's published environmental envelope is IP54 with an operating humidity ceiling of 70% RH and an upper operating temperature well below sauna conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Used only to support a negative judgment: the leading inspection quadruped is not rated for an 80-95°C sauna or a saturated steam room.

instances.label: Scheduled full loss-prevention/operational compliance audit at an assigned store (big-box, grocery or specialty chain): walk sales floor, stockroom, receiving dock and cash office; review cash-handling, refund/void, key-control and audit paperwork; verify CCTV, EAS pedestals and alarm systems are functioning; complete a scored audit form; debrief the store manager and file a corrective-action plan.

Unannounced spot-check / shrink walkthrough: verify high-theft merchandise is protected (locked cases, spider wraps, EAS tags applied), check backroom and compactor/trash areas for concealment, confirm emergency and receiving doors are secured and alarmed, observe register and fitting-room controls, then give verbal feedback and a short written exception list.

Visit triggered by an incident or high-shrink flag: sit with store management to review exception reports and CCTV footage, interview associates about a suspected internal theft or procedural breakdown, walk the area involved, verify prior corrective actions were implemented, and document findings for the investigation file.

Coaching/training visit: deliver an LP awareness or new-policy briefing to associates, watch procedures being performed live (opening/closing, cash pickups, deliveries, self-checkout intervention) and correct technique in the moment, coach the store manager on accountability for prior audit misses.

New-store, remodel or seasonal-readiness visit: verify installed physical security equipment against company standards (camera placement and views, EAS pedestal function and tuning, safe and key control, alarm zones, lighting), test devices, note punch-list defects for vendors, and sign off on readiness.

sources.system: Badger Technologies Retail InSpect / multipurpose grocery robot
sources.title: Badger Technologies robots working 6 Vallarta Supermarkets - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Badger Technologies' Retail InSpect robot autonomously traverses grocery store aisles during trading hours to detect floor hazards and out-of-stock items, alerting staff; it is deployed commercially at chains such as Vallarta Supermarkets and Woodman's Markets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-store safety/hazard patrol of a retail sales floor. It shares the setting (an open trading retail store) and the walk-and-observe element of an LP store visit, but it only reports floor hazards and stock gaps on the sales floor; it does not inspect the cash office, receiving door, security equipment or paperwork, interview staff, or produce a compliance audit with corrective actions, so completion does not transfer.

sources.title: Simbe Introduces Improved Tally 4.0 Shelf-Scanning Robot - The Shelby Report
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally is an autonomous shelf-scanning mobile robot deployed at scale in retail chains that audits shelf conditions for pricing accuracy and planogram compliance and reports exceptions to store teams.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated in-store compliance auditing (merchandising standards). It demonstrates autonomous navigation of a live store and generation of an exception report, but the audited items are shelf labels and product facings, not loss-prevention controls (key control, cash handling, CCTV/EAS function, secured doors), and it cannot debrief or coach management.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor security robot performs scheduled and on-demand autonomous patrols and facility checks in enterprise buildings, flagging anomalies such as open doors or unbadged people, with remote human specialists taking over when an anomaly is detected.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous indoor security patrol and facility check inside a structured human work facility. It covers the 'walk the premises and note security exceptions' fragment of an LP visit, but it checks a premapped route for anomalies rather than auditing procedural compliance, reviewing documentation and footage, or coaching staff.

sources.title: How the K5 Robot Patrols Without Human Help - Knightscope
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 autonomous security robot patrols mapped properties such as parking lots, campuses and shopping centers without hands-on human oversight, streaming detections to a remote security operations center.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous security patrol of commercial property. It establishes reliable autonomous presence and surveillance at retail-adjacent sites, but a patrol robot records and reports observations; it performs none of the inspection, documentation review, testing, interviewing or reporting that constitutes a loss-prevention compliance visit.

instances.label: Early-stage reconnaissance walkover of a vacant former industrial/commercial parcel (Phase I/II-style): overgrown, fenced lot with debris piles, abandoned drums, stained pavement, AST/UST vents, surface staining and distressed vegetation. Specialist walks the parcel, photographs and logs indicators of releases, and forms findings on environmental damage.

Interior inspection of derelict on-site structures: dark, cluttered, partially collapsed former plant buildings, basements, tank rooms and process areas. Opening doors, climbing stairs, looking into sumps and floor drains, identifying asbestos, PCB transformers and abandoned chemical containers.

Periodic progress inspection during active remediation: excavation and contaminated-soil removal, stockpiles, haul trucks, dust suppression and erosion controls. Verify extent/depth of work against the remediation work plan, photo-document conditions, and report progress and deviations.

Routine status round of on-site remediation equipment and controls at a treatment compound taken as found: SVE/air-sparge blowers, groundwater treatment skid gauges and readings, cap/cover integrity, fencing and signage; log readings, flag anomalies (leaks, overheating, damage).

Groundwater/vapor monitoring point work and oversight of sampling crews: unlocking and opening well caps, gauging depth to water, purging and collecting samples, labeling and chain-of-custody handling, field notes in a vacant lot or roadside well nest.

Inspection inside an operating, institution-controlled facility with an ongoing release assessment or remediation: active industrial plant, rail yard, port terminal or landfill/transfer station with known layout, maintained access roads and standard equipment; check for leaks, emissions, spill areas, containment and cleanup status.

sources.system: Percepto Air Max OGI / Percepto AIM drone-in-a-box
sources.title: Autonomous OGI Drones now Alternative Test Method for EPA Subpart OOOOa, OOOOb
sources.claim: Percepto's autonomous drone-in-a-box optical gas imaging system was approved by the US EPA as an Alternative Test Method, authorizing fully remote autonomous emissions (environmental release) inspections for federal compliance at oil and gas sites; already deployed across US basins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: regulatory leak/emissions inspection. It is a site inspection that detects and documents environmental releases with an output accepted by a regulator in place of a human inspector's, performed on institution-controlled industrial premises comparable to a facility where a brownfield specialist assesses environmental damage.

sources.system: Percepto AIM with Percepto Air drone-in-a-box
sources.title: Inspecting and Monitoring Industrial Sites Using AIM - Percepto
sources.claim: At ICL Dead Sea, previously manual inspections of site assets (electric grid, pipes, piles) were converted to automated drone-in-a-box inspection rounds managed by Percepto AIM with no human involvement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine industrial site inspection rounds. Same act of walking/flying a site to observe and document asset and ground conditions, performed on institution-controlled premises.

sources.system: Spot with Orbit and gas/thermal payloads
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot ran autonomous inspection rounds across a 40-acre midstream gas plant performing anomaly detection, thermal inspection and gauge reading, and during one autonomous round detected a combustible gas plume from a pinhole leak.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous facility inspection rounds with leak and equipment anomaly detection. Comparable to a site manager's round checking treatment equipment, gauges and signs of releases inside a controlled facility.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics and DroneDeploy (customer: Turner Construction)
sources.title: Turner Construction Uses Ground Robots to Cut Inspection Time by Over 95 Percent
sources.claim: Turner Construction uses Spot on routes mapped in DroneDeploy that the robot follows autonomously overnight, capturing repeatable 360-degree progress documentation of an active jobsite that is compared against BIM to detect deviations, replacing manual progress photo walks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: construction progress documentation walks. Monitoring cleanup progress on a remediation site is the same act of repeated site walkover, photo documentation and comparison of as-built conditions against the plan, in an equally dynamic, debris-strewn outdoor/indoor work site.

sources.system: FieldAI Field Foundation Models on Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.title: How FieldAI and Boston Dynamics Made Robot Autonomy Practical on Construction Sites
sources.claim: FieldAI foundation models let Spot execute inspection, mapping and monitoring missions on active, constantly changing construction sites without prior maps, GPS or predefined routes, with customers reporting over 90 percent reductions in inspection and documentation time and fleet-wide rollouts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous jobsite inspection and progress scanning. Establishes map-free autonomous traversal and data capture in an unstructured, day-to-day changing site comparable to an active remediation earthwork site.

sources.developer: AtkinsRealis with Sellafield Ltd / Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Remotely operated robot deployed at Sellafield - World Nuclear News
sources.claim: Robotic inspection inside contaminated legacy nuclear buildings at Sellafield is carried out with a Spot robot operated remotely by specialists, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hazardous legacy-building characterisation. Shows that inspection inside contaminated, cluttered derelict structures is still teleoperated, so it cannot support autonomous completion of derelict-building inspection.

sources.system: DJI Dock drones managed by FlytBase (The Drone Centre)
sources.title: How UAE Waste Management Authority Enhances Facility Operations using Autonomous Drones
sources.claim: A UAE waste management authority deployed DJI docks with FlytBase software at multiple waste facilities, providing round-the-clock autonomous surveillance flights with hazard detection, hazardous material detection and volumetric analysis of waste, replacing routine manual inspections of hazardous areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous environmental monitoring at a waste facility. Volumetric measurement of material and detection of hazardous conditions is the same kind of observation a site manager makes when assessing damage or tracking cleanup at an institution-controlled site.
